milestones.description: This milestone defines the foundation for an access-based enterprise trial capability for CoCounsel Tax by finalizing TFMS-specific requirements, clarifying product and platform responsibilities, and aligning on a scalable Enterprise Trials approach. Its purpose is to enable digitally initiated and configurable trials, support a seamless trial-to-paid conversion with no service interruption, and establish a standardized onboarding model that reduces manual processes and prepares product teams for future integration.

This feature replaces the manual day-count input with a calendar-based end date picker in the Salesforce trial creation UI. Reps will select a specific end date directly from a calendar, giving them precise, intuitive control over when the trial ends.

For GLLF and MLF accounts, the calendar picker must enforce a maximum initial trial period of 60 days from the trial start date. Reps may select any end date within the 1–60 day window, but the system must prevent selection or saving of any date that exceeds this limit. This enforcement must be segment-aware — other segments must not be affected by GLLF/MLF-specific rules.

The calendar-based date picker also applies at every extension event, replacing any manual day-count input at the point of extension

The objective is to transition all segments to the Salesforce‑based Enterprise Trial system as the primary solution. Trial strategists will continue to support complex, high‑touch scenarios.
Operational Mechanics: Bulk contact upload is available (limits still to be confirmed). Multi‑location trials remain a per‑account manual process. Usage reporting in Salesforce is now active and sharable.
Volume Benchmark: MLF executed ~1,800 managed trials last year, with ~574 extensions—highlighting the operational scale this migration must support.

Add the Technical Support phone number for West, UK, CARS and AEM region to the existing support contact information so customers have a direct phone option for urgent technical issues. The phone contact should display the below numbers for the regions: US, UK, Canada, AEM

This feature enables sales reps to add one or more eligible products to an already-active GLLF or MLF Enterprise Trial directly from the trial record in Salesforce. When a product is added mid-trial, entitlements must be provisioned seamlessly via TFMS for all users on the trial — both those who have already activated and those who have been invited but not yet activated.

Eligible products in scope are existing bundle offerings used by the GLLF and MLF segments: Westlaw, Practical Law, and Co-Counsel. Simplicity with Deadline Assistant is explicitly out of scope for this phase as it is not onboarded onto the Enterprise Trial system.

Adding a product mid-trial must not trigger duplicate or re-triggered welcome emails to existing trial users via Eloqua.

milestones.description:
Scope

Establish a standardized AI security governance model to ensure all AI capabilities are consistently assessed, reviewed, monitored, and remediated across the lifecycle. This includes defining intake criteria for security reviews, executing secure AI assessments on new features, and enabling operational monitoring and remediation processes to manage risk in production.

Scope
Assess CoCounsel’s current security posture against applicable regulatory and AI-specific standards to identify control gaps and establish a clear baseline for compliance readiness. This includes performing structured gap assessments against SOC 2 Type 2, ISO 27001, and ISO 42001 frameworks.

Business Outcomes
Clear understanding of current compliance posture across key frameworks
Early identification of control gaps impacting audit and certification readiness
Improved ability to prioritize remediation efforts based on risk and compliance impact
Increased confidence from leadership in readiness for regulatory and audit requirements
Stronger alignment with industry standards for AI and security governance

Purpose
This ensures that every service in CoCounsel Next has a clear, named owner, a functioning on-call rota, and a documented escalation path. When something goes wrong in production, there should never be any ambiguity about who responds.
Scope
• Service ownership — a named owner and assignment group (Eng, SRE etc.) recorded for every service
• On-call rota — defined, published, and kept current
• Escalation path — specific named individuals documented and accessible to anyone who might need them

Scope

Enable CoCounsel to effectively communicate its security, legal, and operational posture to customers by providing clear, consistent documentation and ensuring alignment across Customer Trust, Product Engineering, and Labs. This includes delivering core artifacts and preparing responses to anticipated customer questions.

Purpose

Ensures that all changes to the CoCounsel Next production environment — whether code deployments, infrastructure changes, or feature flag modifications — are tracked, owned, and reversible. It is the highest priority milesonte for GA readiness.

Scope

•  Deployment tracking — every production deployment has a corresponding ServiceNow change record and a named owner

•  Feature flag governance — flag changes are auditable and owned

•  Rollback capability — the Service Management team can execute a rollback independently, without engineering support

Out of Scope

The mechanics of how deployments are built or automated (this sits with Engineering). This milestone is concerned with process, ownership, and documentation around changes — not the technical implementation of the pipeline itself.

Dependencies

•  Engineering team to confirm deployment process and provide SM access to execute rollbacks

•  ServiceNow team to confirm change record process and any integration requirements

Purpose

Ensures that when something goes wrong in production, the team knows about it immediately, knows what to do, and has practiced doing it. It covers the flow from alert to incident, the runbooks needed to respond, and a hands-on gameday to validate readiness.

Scope

•  ServiceNow integration — all production issues result in a tracked incident, whether via manual or automated alert-to-incident flow

•  Runbook library — documented, peer-reviewed response guides for the top anticipated failure scenarios

•  Gameday — a hands-on rehearsal of incident response, not a theoretical discussion

Out of Scope

Monitoring and alerting configuration (covered in the Monitoring / Alerting) assumes alerts exist and focuses on what happens after one fires.

Dependencies

•  Monitoring / Alerting — alerts must exist before the incident flow can be validated

•  ServiceNow team — to confirm incident creation process and access

•  Engineering team — to participate in gameday and review runbooks for accuracy
Across CIO (ISRM, SM, Platform Engineering) identify the deliverables, dependencies and requirements to support the CoCo Next rollout.  These will form the 'plan' for delivery.

Purpose
This ensures CoCounsel Next has been tested at realistic load levels, that known breaking points and capacity risks are understood and tracked, and that an ongoing process exists to review and adjust as usage grows.
Scope
• Load testing — CoCounsel Next load tests run concurrently with LSM scale tests, at expected and near-term peak load
• Capacity risk tracking — Mercury limits and other major risks are understood, documented, and owned
• LSM Scale Team engagement — approach and capacity validated with the LSM Scale Team
• Ongoing review — periodic review of production usage and behaviour, with tests adjusted accordingly

Scope
Ensure AI capabilities are ready for General Availability (GA) by addressing key operational risks and establishing minimum security and operational standards for launch. This includes remediating critical protocol issues and defining ISRM guardrails to support consistent and secure AI ESE launches.

Business Outcomes
Reduced risk of security issues at product launch
Improved consistency and control across AI capability releases
Clear expectations for Product Engineering on security and operational requirements
Increased confidence from leadership in GA readiness
Stronger alignment between ISRM and product teams on launch standards

risks.title: Tool duplication and fragmented adoption across ICFR tooling ecosystem
risks.description: Multiple tools (Protecht, ADO, SharePoint, legacy repositories, DoubleCheck) currently support overlapping ICFR activities without a clear target-state architecture, risking continued duplication and fragmented adoption even after the transformation.

risks.title: Change fatigue among control owners participating in ICFR transformation
risks.description: Control owners are already subject to multiple initiatives and may experience change fatigue as new ICFR processes, controls, tooling, and certifications are introduced.

risks.title: PwC may refuse to use internal ICFR tools for audit interactions
risks.description: The external auditor (PwC) has previously been hesitant to use internal tools, and may continue to resist adopting Protecht or related platforms for evidence requests and status updates.

risks.title: Over-scoping of ICFR due to conservative posture
risks.description: The organization may continue to define an overly broad ICFR scope, including excessive controls and application coverage, due to conservative risk and audit postures, despite transformation efforts to rationalize.

risks.title: Non-integrated access systems and third-party portals may weaken access governance
risks.description: Some systems are not integrated with SailPoint and rely on manual processes or third-party portals, creating potential gaps in provisioning, certification, and deprovisioning controls within the ICFR scope.

risks.title: Inconsistent evidence quality across ICFR controls
risks.description: Evidence supporting ICFR controls may vary in quality, completeness, and standardization, which can undermine audit readiness and increase rework during testing and external reviews.

risks.title: Program sprawl and excessive stakeholder model may dilute focus and slow decisions
risks.description: The ICFR transformation program may expand its scope or stakeholder base excessively, resulting in complex governance, slow decision-making, and blurred accountability.

risks.title: Limited stakeholder availability may delay ICFR design and implementation
risks.description: Key finance, operations, business, compliance, IT, and audit stakeholders may not have sufficient time to participate in workshops, reviews, and approvals, which could slow or stall the design, validation, and implementation of the modernized ICFR operating model.

risks.title: Competing business priorities may reduce participation from control owners and functional leads
risks.description: Control owners and functional leaders may prioritize other initiatives or operational demands over participation in the ICFR transformation activities, reducing timely engagement in design, testing, and adoption.

risks.title: Inconsistent existing documentation may increase effort required for assessment and standardization
risks.description: Current SOX and ICFR documentation is inconsistent in quality, format, and completeness, which may increase the complexity and effort needed to perform current-state assessment, gap analysis, and standardization.

risks.title: Change resistance may slow adoption of new ICFR processes, templates, and tools
risks.description: Control owners, process teams, and other stakeholders may resist changes to established ICFR processes, documentation standards, and tooling, slowing adoption of the future-state operating model.

risks.title: Technology dependencies or approval delays may impact implementation timing for system enablement
risks.description: If supporting technology changes, integrations, or new tools require extended architecture, security, or procurement approvals, implementation of system-enabled ICFR capabilities may be delayed.

risks.title: Delays in AWS AMS region build-out and supporting TR infrastructure may compress schedule and slip migrations
risks.description: The initial AMS region build-out by AWS for Sydney, plus the subsequent Thomson Reuters infrastructure build (NAS, Active Directory, data connection endpoints, Oracle pattern application, etc.), is already delayed due to blocks on the AWS side and past resourcing constraints in Platform Engineering. This is causing planned work to "concertina" into the second half of 2026. If AWS and TR infrastructure are not available when needed, application migrations (batches 1–3 and pre-work for CAMS) may be delayed, reducing schedule buffer and potentially pushing the overall Sydney colo exit beyond the currently targeted dates (end of 2026 for non‑CAMS apps and mid‑2027 for CAMS and dilapidation).

risks.title: Unproven NAS/FSx integration and user drive-mounting model may cause delays once AMS is available
risks.description: The planned NAS solution (e.g., NetApp FSx) in AMS must support both application servers and end users who access content via mapped drives (F: drive). This pattern, particularly via Zscaler and cloud-based CIFS/SMB shares, has not been fully proven for the Sydney legal content workloads and is considered "not straightforward." If this integration does not work as expected, significant troubleshooting and re-design may be required.

risks.title: Active Directory and IAM design for AMS region may be delayed or misaligned with app needs
risks.description: Active Directory (AD) and IAM support for applications in AMS Sydney has not yet been fully designed or agreed with the enterprise IAM (EAD) team. The apps today rely on enterprise AD, and it is unclear what, if any, new AD infrastructure or domain controllers are required in AMS and who will operate them. If AD/IAM design and ownership are not resolved early, application access and authentication could become a late-breaking blocker.

risks.title: CAMS migration depends on completion and deployment of new GCS-based component and may not meet mid-2027 Sydney exit target
risks.description: CAMS migration (Batch 4) is dependent on a new GCS-based component and related integrations being completed and fully deployed into production. The component work is ongoing, with differing views between the engineering lead (Varadaraja) and his manager on what can be achieved by end of year (build vs. full deployment and user cutover). If the GCS-based component is not delivered and adopted as planned, CAMS migration may not start in time to meet the current mid-2027 Sydney colo exit date.

risks.title: Compressed schedule with most migration work in 2H 2026 leaves limited buffer for issues
risks.description: Due to earlier slippage of infrastructure and preparatory tasks that were originally planned for 2025–early 2026 ("the green bit"), much of the remaining migration work for non-CAMS applications is now concentrated in the second half of 2026. Buffer and contingency have effectively been used up, and the project is considered "very risky" because everything is happening later than planned.

risks.title: VMware/Solaris migrations are priority/dependency over Colo Exit activities
risks.description: VMware/Solaris migrations are priority/dependency over Colo Exit activities with some of the migrations requiring new builds as some of the Solaris version are to old to migrate from WMware to Hyper-V.

risks.title: Abacus/Barossa - Azure AVD environment provisioning and LandingZone automation may delay migration
risks.description: Because the Abacus/Barossa Azure AVD environment is a brand new environment that is not yet covered by existing automation workflows, there is a risk that the Permit to Build (P2B) / CSA approval workflow and LandingZone automation steps will cause delays or misconfiguration. Gordon Aitchison must submit the non-prod P2B for Archon, then close his CSA approval task as "incomplete" and separately email the ticket details to the LandingZone team. If this is not followed, existing automation may build the wrong infrastructure, requiring cleanup. In addition, the LandingZone team must split and update code to support the new environment, which Bill Richardson estimates will take up to one sprint (~2 weeks) but cannot yet commit to an exact timeline. Any delay in these activities will delay Azure subscription setup, Active Directory work, and subsequent installation and testing for the Abacus/Barossa migration.

risks.title: HighQ: CSPP – Microsoft program requirement for WOPI (8 week expected time) – request submitted
risks.description:
For continuity of service within the new HighQ Azure Gov environment of our Open-in-Office-for-the-Web/WOPI integration, we are required to submit a CSPP environment change request to Microsoft. 
 
This request has been submitted and normally this process should take 4-5 weeks for Microsoft to complete, however, they informed us May 22 that, due to issues on their side with Office deployment via CSPP, this could now take up to 8 weeks. 
 
Despite detailed conversations with Microsoft over the last 3 months in relation to this service, we weren't previously informed of this requirement, however, we are doing all we can to expedite execution via Microsoft as quickly as possible.

risks.title: Infeasibility of effective governance with 110+ Datadog organizations
risks.description: The team questioned whether effective governance is feasible with over 110 Datadog organizations. The group agreed that governance is significantly harder at this scale and that deeper analysis and architectural discussion are required to determine a sustainable governance model.

risks.title: Insufficient Datadog monitor metadata blocks scalable cleanup
risks.description: Tax, Corporate, and Legal teams have indicated that current Datadog inventory exports do not include critical metadata such as "who created the monitor", "who the monitor is assigned to", and "when the monitor last fired". Dominique reported that Tax explicitly called this a "showstopper" for performing ongoing cleanup of monitors without Asset IDs. Without this metadata, teams cannot efficiently group, prioritize, or assign remediation work across hundreds or thousands of monitors.

risks.title: Significant Asset ID coverage gaps in Datadog monitors
risks.description: Based on a February snapshot, about 25% of Datadog monitors lack an associated Asset ID. The team highlighted this as a critical data quality gap and a priority risk, and noted the need for a repeatable approach and ongoing inventory refresh to improve Asset ID coverage.

risks.title: Program timelines and Phase 1 schedule not yet defined
risks.description: The team acknowledged that target timelines for Phase 1 deliverables and overall Datadog Hygiene program reporting are not yet defined. Timelines are required for reporting, and work needs to be time‑boxed via a backlog, but specific dates have not been set.

risks.title: Alert-threshold hygiene may be misreported if synthetic monitors are not excluded
risks.description: Nick and Dominique discussed that a "large chunk" of monitors show no alert threshold configured. Dominique clarified that, based on review with Tax, many of these are synthetic monitors, for which a traditional threshold is not expected. Current counting and reporting of "monitors without thresholds" does not filter out synthetics, which can overstate the problem and distort hygiene metrics.

risks.title: Potential negative impacts of reducing the number of Datadog organizations
risks.description: The program is considering whether to reduce the current number of Datadog organizations (110+). High complexity and several risks have been acknowledged, including possible loss of historical data, anomaly detection model resets, and AI/MCP rate‑limit or capacity impacts if organizations are consolidated without a carefully designed approach.

risks.title: Misalignment of Datadog default maturity scorecards with Thomson Reuters standards
risks.description: The team is exploring whether existing Datadog maturity scorecards can be used to measure observability maturity. Datadog’s default scorecards are generic and likely not aligned to Thomson Reuters’ internal observability and monitoring standards. If they are adopted without proper alignment or customization, measurements of maturity may be misleading or inconsistent across teams.

risks.title: Insufficient engineering and architecture participation in the core working group

risks.title: Missing or blank Datadog Monitor IDs in ServiceNow payloads

risks.title: Data quality issues in correlation IDs and Datadog–ServiceNow mappings prevent reliable analytics

risks.title: Absence of minimum alert standards constrains remediation

risks.title: JFrog Artifactory Issues Blocking CI/CD Pipelines (Rate Limits & npm Metadata)
risks.description: Issue Summary: SafeSend Project team highlighted the criticality of resolving the package-building issue to ensure the project stays on track for its July delivery deadlines. Without this resolution, development and testing will remain blocked, jeopardizing the timeline. The team is trying to identify the right person to escalate or resolve the issue urgently

risks.title: Function App VNet Integration and Access Issues:
risks.description:
1.	Issue Identification:
•	[Pramod] the issue was investigated by multiple teams, including the Landing Zone Team, the ISRM Team, and their internal team, and it was confirmed that the problem is not related to networking.
•	A support ticket was raised with Microsoft regarding the severity A issue, and Microsoft identified that the problem was due to SKU configuration deviations.
2.	SKU Configuration Deviation:
•	There is a difference in the infrastructure configuration between Central Region and East US 2 Region. The infrastructure available in the Central Region is not fully available in East US 2, which caused the deviation.
3.	Current Status:
•	The deviation issue has been addressed, and the team has deployed the necessary changes.
•	The team is currently testing the infrastructure by applying load to determine whether the application will break or handle the load successfully.
4.	Next Steps: [Pramod] will provide a status update by Monday, 08 June once the teams complete testing and investigation of the infrastructure under load.

risks.title: Cutover and rollback planning for production migration may be incomplete before migration window
risks.description: The RunBook_Prod sheet shows that cutover and rollback planning tasks (including detailed cutover steps and rollback actions for application, database, storage, and domain changes) are marked as 'Not yet Started'. These activities are essential to safely execute the production migration and to revert changes if issues occur.

risks.title: Production storage and table migrations may fail or overrun due to untested migration service setup
risks.description: Production storage blob and table migrations depend on deploying a migration service and VM/AKS-based tooling (AzCopy, scripts, jobs) during April 17–27, 2026. The RunBook_Prod notes that the service for storage migration needs to be deployed and that Ravindra must update the storage migration plan with prerequisites and tasks. If these prerequisites are not ready or adequately tested, the production storage migrations may fail or take longer than the planned window.

risks.title: Key Vault secret migration and validation may delay production deployment readiness
risks.description: In the RunBook_Prod, key vault secret migration tasks (creating target Key Vault, bulk secret migration, ATUM deployment, and secret validation) are all marked as 'Not yet Started'. Dev notes from earlier environments indicate that application deployment depends on Key Vault being updated and operational. If key vault tasks slip, production deployment readiness may be delayed.

risks.title: Incomplete CI/CD migration from Azure DevOps to GitHub Actions could impact non-production DevOps migration timeline
risks.description: The DevOps Migration Phase (Non-Prod) indicates that ADO to GitHub migration is in progress with several outstanding tasks such as bulk creation of CI/CD pipelines as GitHub Actions workflows, validation of builds and artifacts, and full end-to-end dry runs. Notes highlight constraints around JFrog version updates and limitations with variable group mapping, requiring conversion of variable groups into YAML files.

risks.title: Wildcard certificate and domain management constraints may impact SSL and customer subdomain strategy
risks.description: The QA and Dev runbooks note ongoing POCs for SSL certificates via Venafi and for adapting existing domains, as well as discussion around wildcard certificates for customer-specific subdomains (thousands of potential subdomains). TR standards typically do not accept wildcard certificates, requiring exceptions or design changes. Although one historical RAID entry indicates the team decided not to proceed with wildcard certificates, the broader production SSL and domain strategy (including potential migration from GoDaddy to AWS Route 53) still requires alignment and impact analysis.

risks.title: Datadog training and integration may not be completed before production migration
risks.description: Datadog training is a prerequisite for setting up monitoring integrations for the new TR Azure subscriptions. Notes indicate that key tasks for Datadog IaC, RUM, and APM monitoring cannot be fully defined or executed until SafeSend and TR staff complete training and understand TR Datadog standards. If training and integration are delayed, monitoring for infrastructure and applications in the new TR Azure tenant may not be ready before or during production migration.

risks.title: Service principal (SPN) strategy across environments may increase cost or operational overhead

risks.title: Fallback Area Path behavior defaulting to root when mapping fails
risks.description: If Area Path mapping fails during ADO work item creation, work items will land in the root Area Path. The team has not yet formally confirmed that this fallback behavior is acceptable for MVP operations.

risks.description: There is a risk that teams will attempt to synchronize too much data between Salesforce, ServiceNow, and ADO rather than focusing on controlled, intentional integrations.

risks.title: Change‑management‑driven validation and business go‑live may significantly lag technical MVP
risks.description: Technical MVP for Salesforce–ADO (and later ServiceNow) is on track, but validation testing and business go‑live are being planned as part of a separate CSS change‑management process led by Darren Thurin’s team. Current indications are that this process could add roughly two months between technical readiness and agent rollout, with unclear ownership of validation and limited early exposure of flows to stakeholders.

risks.title: Data quality gaps in manual cross‑referencing
risks.description: Current manual cross‑referencing between Salesforce, ServiceNow, Azure DevOps and other systems lacks reliable identifiers and source data (such as source system IDs and URLs). In this model, a single customer can be left in a hybrid state for an extended period (some users/products federated, others not). During the May 29, 2026 weekly status meeting, Peter Grigoriou and Jeff Olson noted that many customers may be comfortable remaining in this hybrid state, while Harvarinder Batth expressed concern that once such configurations are in place they may persist "for the next 10 or 20 years," effectively becoming long-lived technical debt and potentially creating security gaps if customers assume all access is federated and centrally controlled.

Sales leaders (Kristine and Marie) agree with this direction, but the SAP product team (owned by Kyle in the Amy Hutsell group) has not yet committed to delivering the required feature to stop creating new OnePass accounts. In the interim (next ~1.5 months), new accounts continue to be created on OnePass, requiring manual migration before MCP can be enabled and adding operational overhead and noise. Pages listing thousands of customer URLs are taking a very long time to load and intermittently timing out, which in turn causes errors and delays when the customer SSO team attempts to configure new CIAM SSO connections or modify existing ones. These issues are affecting not only CIAM migration work but any customer SSO configuration activity that relies on Ping, and are causing setup cycles to take significantly longer than expected. Although a workaround exists and some remediation work is planned (including a change being deployed the night of June 5, 2026), there is a risk that these problems persist or recur, creating ongoing friction and delay in enabling SSO for CIAM migrations.

Requests arrive via a new form and require checking whether accounts are SSO or local, obtaining customer approval to migrate to CIAM, and then handing off to Kim for inclusion in nightly migration waves. There is no weekend/holiday coverage in place yet, and Harv is considering checking requests hourly or every two hours. Leadership explicitly called out that Harv is a potential single point of failure and that early in the process there could be 72-hour windows (e.g., long weekends) where customers receive no response. This could undermine the opportunity to capitalize on strong inbound demand from Anthropic MCP users who are "fish wanting to jump into the boat."

There is a risk that HighQ migrations slip beyond the life of the central SSO migration team or are indefinitely delayed, leaving a large block of connections on legacy SSO and undermining CIAM migration objectives.

risks.title: Ethical walls — agentic AI poses breach risk if permissions not enforced correctly
risks.description: Agentic AI can traverse large volumes of content and generate derived artefacts that may unintentionally combine restricted sources. Ethical walls must be enforced based on the content accessed during generation, not just on the appearance of the output. Derived content must inherit permissions from its sources, and admin privileges must not grant agents broader content access.

risks.title: Multiple blocking architectural decisions unresolved (identity, admin tool, FGA, CIAM)
risks.description: Four interdependent architectural decisions remain unresolved and are blocking the start of build: (1) where the admin tool will be hosted, (2) how CIAM enforcement will operate, (3) which user identity (Prism GUID vs EUID) will be used by Auth0 FGA, and (4) how the FGA store will be structured. Until these are decided, downstream design and implementation cannot progress.

risks.title: IaC deployer feature gaps in Cumulus
risks.description: The Cumulus infrastructure-as-code (IaC) deployer lacked feature parity and was not in sync with current source code changes, forcing manual infrastructure provisioning.

risks.title: Blue / Green deployer approval delays
risks.description: Cumulus blue/green deployments can fail if the "green" approval is delayed, causing deployment failures and requiring re-runs.

risks.title: Difficulty troubleshooting Cumulus installations due to incomplete logging
risks.description: Logging for Cumulus installations and pipeline creations with multiple assets can be lost or is hard to locate, making it difficult to troubleshoot failed installations.

risks.title: Cumulus installation on Prod CI/CD account 386694349529
risks.description: Cumulus was not yet installed on the critical production CI/CD account (386694349529), blocking automated deployments for CoCounsel.

risks.title: Cumulus CPI inflation runs assets sequentially instead of in parallel
risks.description: The CPI inflation process runs multiple assets sequentially rather than in parallel, extending execution time by several minutes per run.

risks.title: Helm deployer feature gaps in Cumulus
risks.description: The Cumulus Helm deployer lacked feature parity and was not in sync with current source code changes, requiring services to be deployed manually and halting some Cumulus adoption.

risks.title: Cumulus UI dashboard Lambda failure on null deployment status
risks.description: The Cumulus UI dashboard Lambda fails when a deployment record has a null status message, causing the dashboard to error and preventing blue/green deployment approvals via the UI.

risks.title: Incorrect GovCloud pipeline links in Cumulus UI dashboard
risks.description: GovCloud pipeline links shown in the Cumulus UI dashboard used the wrong host, requiring users to manually navigate to the correct pipelines.

risks.title: Cumulus multi-region support blocker
risks.description: A Cumulus defect blocked correct operation of multi-region pipelines needed for CoCounsel and related workloads.

risks.title: Cloudflare ingress blocked by Cumulus deployspec for Terraform
risks.description: The cumulus-deployspec-cloudflare (Terraform) implementation blocked creation of required public ingress (incoming calls) for CoCounsel and CARI services.

risks.title: EKS deployer feature gaps in Cumulus
risks.description: The Cumulus EKS deployer lacked feature parity with source code changes, forcing manual deployment of EKS-based services and temporarily halting some Cumulus usage.

risks.title: Terraform deployer feature gaps in Cumulus
risks.description: The Cumulus Terraform deployer lacked feature parity with current infrastructure definitions, requiring teams to automate Terraform deployments outside Cumulus (e.g., via GitHub Actions).

risks.title: ServiceNow GovCloud setup and inventory integration stability
risks.description: Ongoing issues with the ServiceNow GovCloud setup, including asset discovery challenges, vendor engagement, and asset tagging; a manual workaround is currently in place. Discovery for FedRAMP AWS GovCloud accounts is still not functioning as expected, requiring repeated vendor cases and engineering access changes.

actions.title: Complete ServiceNow GovCloud inventory integration for FedRAMP CoCounsel
actions.description: Drive completion of the ServiceNow GovCloud setup and inventory integration required for FedRAMP audit readiness, coordinating with the vendor and internal engineers until the integration is fully working and evidence is available for auditors.

risks.title: GTM4 Content PROD Cluster Migration
risks.description:
The GTM4 Content PROD environment includes three critical content clusters with high customer dependency. Migrating these clusters requires re‑initializing database replication from scratch, which is time‑consuming and highly sensitive to maintenance windows. There is a risk that replication may not complete within the agreed downtime window. Similar challenges were experienced during the earlier on‑prem to cloud migration, where replication delays caused operational issues.
Additionally, a future GCP content migration is already planned, which may require repeating the same replication process—potentially resulting in two customer downtimes if not carefully planned.
Risk Impact:
Potential extended PROD downtime impacting customers
Increased operational and reputational risk if replication fails or overruns
Need for multiple customer downtimes (current migration + future GCP migration)
Possible schedule changes to GTM4 Phase / Wave execution
Minor cost impact (~$4.5K/month) if clusters are retained longer as‑is, but operational risk outweighs cost considerations.
Risk Probability:
Medium – based on past replication challenges and dependency complexity, pending business decision. 
Current Status / Decision Pending:
Risk logged primarily as a decision risk
Business discussion scheduled to assess tolerance for downtime vs. deferring migration
Final approach may change based on Business Unit agreement
Mitigation / Next Steps:
Review and align with the Business Unit on acceptable downtime and migration approach
Explore deferring migration of these clusters to align with future GCP migration, avoiding double downtime
Document final business decision in ADO and update RAID accordingly (close or re‑categorize risk) 
Owner
GTM Business

issues.title: Remediate Boleto Generation Backlog (RITM0143783) — Company Codes 2053/2060 (Apr 17–May 11)
issues.description:
Objective: Resolve pending boleto backlog to restore full payment processing capability. Current Situation: - Issue fixed for new invoices - Historical invoices (~backlog) missing boletos - Root cause related to upstream payment processing failure Problem: Uncertainty if bank received payment files Expected Outcome: - Bank confirms file receipt - Clear recovery approach defined and executed Activities: - Confirm file receipt with bank - If received → validate processing - If NOT received → define reprocessing or manual creation - Execute agreed solution with Finance Dependency: - Bank confirmation Risk: Operational and financial reconciliation delay.

Detailed Technical Description
We need to remediate the historical backlog of customer invoices where no boleto was generated during Apr 17–May 11, impacting Brazil Company Codes 2053 and 2060. [S&O All Ha...Recording | Video]

Confirmed technical context and findings (from the emails):

Forward processing is already stable: Ana Paula confirmed the fix that was deployed to production (ADO#1271143 moved via CHG0228804 on May 12) is successful, and boletos generated from May 12 onward are being processed correctly.
Historical backlog remains unresolved: Even though processing is stable after May 12, the backlog of invoices between Apr 17–May 11 still needs a remediation plan and closure. 
Next step requires bank/CNAB assessment: The next action is to assess whether the CNAB file can be reprocessed with the bank for invoices that did not have a boleto generated in that period. If reprocessing is not possible, the backlog invoices will require manual boleto creation in the Citibank portal by the Collections team. 
Scope/volume stated: The email estimates approximately 1,700 invoices in this period (with future due dates) are impacted. 
Upstream ownership is still unclear: Your escalation note indicates that upstream ownership for the end-to-end payment request/boleto generation process is not yet clearly assigned, and a single accountable owner is needed to drive remediation and closure
Suggested Definition of Done (DoD):

Confirm and document remediation approach for backlog: CNAB reprocess vs manual creation.
Execute the remediation plan to generate/restore missing boletos for the Apr 17–May 11 invoices.
Provide validation evidence that missing boletos are generated/registered correctly for the backlog invoices
Confirm upstream accountable owner and close the loop for formal closure.

risks.title: Agent Chat go-live may impact SLAs due to untested high-volume routing behavior
risks.description: During the June 11, 2026 Agent Chat gap analysis call, Nitin highlighted that, in the current Vayusphere setup, all chats enter a single queue and are manually picked up by agents, with SMEs able to reassign chats to meet a 6–30 second SLA. In ServiceNow Advanced Work Assignment (AWA), chats are routed automatically based on capacity and skills, with a current 1-minute acceptance window and no equivalent SME override feature. Nitin expressed concern that, without volume testing and routing tuning (e.g., reduced acceptance window, auto-assignment), high chat volumes may not be routed correctly, leading to SLA breaches. He also noted that agents are new to the tool and that SLA exceptions may be needed for 2–3 months during transition. Jakub indicated he is open to SLA exceptions and suggested a phased rollout (e.g., APAC first) and possible parallel run with Vayusphere, but no detailed deployment plan is yet defined.

risks.title: Conversational greeting and fallback workflow may miss 2026-05-07 commitment
risks.description: The team committed to having a more natural, conversational virtual agent greeting, closing, and fallback experience ready by 2026-05-07, based on feedback from leaders (including Marc) that the current Now Assist chat lacks greetings, closing messages, validation, and ticket number sharing. During the 2026-05-05 SNOWNAWA working session, Shariq highlighted that there has been "no meaningful progress" on these conversational workflows, ownership is unclear (who raises the story, what Ashima and developers are working from), and admin access to edit templates is constrained. Although predefined templates and out-of-the-box system topics exist, they are not yet configured to meet the desired experience. If these items are not implemented and tested rapidly, the team may miss the 2026-05-07 target it has "given ourselves" for fixing the greetings and related chat behaviors.

risks.title: Lack of Agent Chat historical and current data in dashboards may impact governance reporting
risks.description: In the June 11, 2026 Agent Chat gap analysis discussion, Nitin noted that the dashboards currently used for governance and reporting rely on Vayusphere data, and that the new Agent Chat dashboard does not yet contain any data. He expressed concern that, until Agent Chat is actively used and/or historical data is migrated, HCL will be unable to produce monthly and hourly trending reports and other governance outputs from the Agent Chat portal. Saket and Nitin also discussed the possibility of migrating historical Vayusphere data into the Agent Chat dashboard, which Prashanth described as a separate data migration effort requiring analysis of tables and columns.

During the April 29, 2026 KB planning meeting, Shariq noted he will not be able to meaningfully progress this work until after the upcoming long weekend and is targeting Tuesday to have an executable plan. risks.title: Zurich upgrade and dev freeze may cause loss or rework of recent virtual agent and agent chat changes
risks.description: The upcoming Zurich upgrade will introduce a dev freeze period (May 8 to June 8) and a clone from production into the development environment. During the May 11, 2026 sync, Vinay explained that to avoid losing in-flight development work (especially virtual agent conversational workflows, plugins, and configuration changes), developers must take backups of update sets before the end of Friday. Srinu confirmed that some changes are already captured in update sets, but others (such as plugin enabling or certain configuration options) are not; these will need to be documented and manually re-applied after the clone. If backups and documentation are incomplete, recent VA and Agent Chat work could be overwritten or require significant rework after the clone, impacting timelines.

risks.title: Copilot live agent handoff and transcript sharing may not meet requirements
risks.description: The team is pivoting to Microsoft 365 Copilot as the interim conversational front end, but the live agent transfer capability from Copilot into ServiceNow Agent Chat has not yet been implemented or tested. Mayank and Shariq emphasized that for a good user experience, the entire Copilot conversation (or at least a useful summary) must be handed over to the ServiceNow live agent so that the agent can see the history and context. Today, the live agent functionality sits fully on the ServiceNow side, and it is unclear whether Copilot can reliably pass conversation history into the ServiceNow interaction/incident or whether an additional topic/API must be built specifically for live agent transfer. Until this is designed and validated, there is a risk that the handoff will be incomplete or fail altogether.

risks.title: Dynamic language translation capability may be lost when moving from Now Assist to Copilot
risks.description: Jakub and Shariq highlighted that the current dynamic language translation feature (used in Agent Chat to support non-English users while routing to English-speaking agents) relies on Now Assist capabilities. As the team pivots to Copilot as the front-end conversational agent, it is unclear whether equivalent dynamic translation will be available or how it will be implemented. Prastuti confirmed that Now Assist is required for the current AI-based real-time translation. If an alternative solution is not put in place, the project could lose the ability to offshore non-English traffic to the main support center while still providing localized experiences to users.

risks.title: Copilot-based solution may not preserve interaction linkage and history in ServiceNow
risks.description: Prastuti raised concern that, with Now Assist, conversational data is attached to the ServiceNow interaction and carried forward to incidents, enabling AWA-based features such as routing users back to the same agent within a time window. She noted that, with Copilot, TR will likely not store Copilot conversations as Virtual Agent conversations in ServiceNow by default. It is uncertain whether Copilot conversations will be linked to interaction/incident records in a way that preserves history and supports existing AWA capabilities (e.g., context-aware routing).

risks.title: Amazon Connect CTI URL misconfiguration may delay IVR demo and cutover

Saket stated that once the correct URL is provided and CTI testing is successful, the team will need an additional 2–3 business days to confirm testing, followed by approximately 10–14 days for the telco/ISP to change the external IVR numbers and perform cutover, with old numbers running in parallel for 2–3 weeks. risks.title: Conversational greeting and fallback workflow may miss 2026-05-15 target due to customization constraints and vendor dependency

Initial review on the prior Thursday suggested that achieving the desired greeting behavior may not be possible purely with out-of-the-box configuration and might require customization. During the May 11, 2026 sync, Vinay cautioned that custom scripting inside Now Assist / Virtual Agent is high risk for future upgrades and generally not recommended without ServiceNow guidance. The team is now dependent on multiple working sessions with the ServiceNow vendor (planned from Tuesday to Friday) to determine whether the required behavior can be achieved via configuration or safe customization. Integrate Akkadia into the FedRAMP boundary without disrupting the Moderate authorization baseline, with full governance and audit readiness.
KRs: SCR approved; SIA completed; architecture updates approved; 3PAO audit with no findings; no authorization impact; controls, evidence, and dependencies tracked to completion with proactive risk management.

Objective 3: Migrate Legal Research data with zero customer impact
Execute a secure transition of all FedRAMP Legal Research data from S3 to Akkadia with disciplined cross‑team delivery.
KRs: 100% data migrated; zero data loss; no customer disruption; post‑migration controls verified; delivery executed across engineering, security, and compliance teams within FY26 EPC funding.

risks.title: GovCloud feature gaps may require Akkadia design adjustments
risks.description: Differences in AWS GovCloud feature availability versus commercial regions may require Akkadia design adjustments. If identified late or complex to resolve, these gaps could impact architecture timelines, delay environment readiness milestones, or limit parity with commercial CoCounsel.

risks.title: Akkadia as largest new FedRAMP risk surface in Packet #2
risks.description: As Akkadia is new to the FedRAMP boundary, late identification of FedRAMP security or architectural gaps for Akkadia could delay GovCloud milestones, slow SCR approval, increase 3PAO remediation cost, and risk continuity of the existing Moderate authorization.

actions.title: Terraform vs. Cumulus Replacement Evaluation
actions.description:
Evaluate whether Terraform can fully replace Cumulus by incrementally refactoring infrastructure code and validating that Terraform can replicate required Cumulus functionality, leveraging existing team expertise.
Approach: Week‑to‑week refactoring and validation; decision made iteratively based on outcomes rather than a one‑time checkpoint.
Outcome: Confirm Terraform as the long‑term solution or identify residual gaps requiring Cumulus.

actions.title: Track architecture decision on ECS Fargate vs Plexus for Akkadia
actions.description: Coordinate and track completion of the architecture decision on whether Akkadia in FedRAMP GovCloud will use ECS Fargate or Plexus, with a goal of finalizing by the end of the week of 2026-05-04, as discussed in the 2026-05-04 planning meeting.

actions.title: Create and assign ServiceNow GovCloud setup and inventory integration stories for Akkadia
actions.description: Create and assign user stories in the current sprint to implement the ServiceNow GovCloud setup and inventory integration tasks for Akkadia, as called out separately from general security control implementation.

actions.title: Coordinate firewall configuration for Akkadia GovCloud with Dalton
actions.description: Continue working with Dalton to complete the required firewall configuration and traffic flows for Akkadia in GovCloud, including confirming whether CoCounsel requests to the public load balancer from private subnets/private IPs require additional configuration on the CoCounsel side.

actions.title: Manage follow-up activities from Akkadia security control gap assessment within the Significant Change process
actions.description: Per the 2026-05-29 FedRAMP Akkadia planning meeting, the Akkadia security control gap assessment is scheduled to start on 2026-05-29 and will be an ongoing activity. Any follow-up actions required for the FedRAMP Significant Change Request (SCR) will be managed as part of that process.

actions.title: Confirm completion of final PRODUCT GovCloud account build for Akkadia
actions.description: Obtain confirmation that the last PRODUCT GovCloud account build required for Akkadia has been completed, so that the PRODUCT account build workstream can be formally wrapped up.
