entities.name: SM AIOps/Event Management (SNOW)
entities.okrs:
SM-2 2.1 AI Reimagine
Objective: Deploy ServiceNow's AIOps and Predictive Intelligence to transform event management processes.
Key Result: # of products where Predictive Intelligence (AIOps) capabilities have been implemented
entities.service_maturity: ["SM-7 | AI Enablement\nSM-7-02 | SNOW Event Management / AI Ops"]

risks.title: Unresolved ServiceNow CI–service association behaviour may block cutover from Datadog incidents
risks.description: During the May 12, 2026 AIOps Product Onboarding regional sync, the team observed that ServiceNow is not associating services with the correct CIs for large applications such as Legal Tracker. Internal analysis suggests that a configurable limit of approximately 1,000 CIs per service causes additional CIs to be handled via dynamic CI groups, which in turn prevents correct service association and grouping. ServiceNow’s consultant (Doug) indicated there are “traverse rules” that might address this but needs to consult CMDB experts. Until a clear recommendation and fix are in place, the Legal Tracker product team considers this a showstopper for disabling Datadog-direct incident creation.

risks.title: Incorrect priority and severity mapping from Datadog to ServiceNow incidents
risks.description: Priority and severity values from Datadog monitors are not yet consistently or correctly mapped into ServiceNow alert and incident fields. Severity has sometimes been populated from unexpected payload fields, custom test fields exist, and the mapping between Datadog alert_priority/alert_type and ServiceNow severity, impact, urgency, and priority is still being designed. If this is not resolved before enabling automated incident creation, incidents may be mis‑prioritized.

risks.title: Lack of monitoring governance and standardized thresholds across products
risks.description: There is no centralized event management practice or monitoring governance. Platform Engineering publishes Datadog policies on SharePoint but does not audit or enforce them. Thresholds and configurations vary by product; 80% of monitors are synthetics with product‑specific thresholds, and 75% of GCC events come from one product (HighQ). Many teams do not understand event threshold concepts (informational/warning/critical).

risks.title: Departure of key AIOps architect (Chris Rutherford) may impact continuity and governance
risks.description: During the 30-Apr-2026 regular sync, Jot and the team thanked Chris Rutherford and noted that he would not be on the project from the following day. Chris has been the primary architect and leadership liaison for the ServiceNow AIOps/Event Management design, including incident priority behaviour, governance model, onboarding approach, and alignment with the Datadog hygiene programme. His departure creates a risk that architectural context, design rationale, and decision history may be lost or diluted, slowing future rule changes, onboarding of new products, and governance maturation.

risks.title: High concentration of noise from HighQ overshadowing other Tier 1 services
risks.description: 75% of GCC monthly events come from a single product (HighQ) out of ~50 Tier 1 products. If this concentration of noise is not addressed, it will continue to dominate GCC workload and may mask important events from other services, even after Event Management is enabled.

risks.title: Datadog and ServiceNow event volume and storage constraints
risks.description: There are concerns about the volume of events if all Datadog accounts send events into ServiceNow. While Datadog does not charge egress fees, ServiceNow storage is finite (e.g., ~4TB per instance), and high event volume could consume storage and impact performance if retention and filtering strategies are not defined.

risks.title: Teams without Event Management access losing visibility during cutover
risks.description: Not all operational teams (e.g., Major Incident team) currently have access to the Event Management module and dashboards. If the legacy Datadog–driven incident creation is disabled before those teams have alternative visibility, they may not see or manage critical events during and after cutover.

risks.title: CI binding from events/alerts to CMDB CIs may not work reliably
risks.description: Despite existing CIs in the CMDB with matching names, ServiceNow’s out‑of‑the‑box CI identification and binding logic is often failing to associate incoming Datadog events/alerts with the correct CI records.

risks.title: Legal Tracker monitor priorities and severities may not align with TR standards needed for AIOps
risks.description: Legal Tracker’s Datadog monitors currently have impact, urgency, and priority configured in Terraform, but those settings may not align with the TR incident priority matrix or with what AIOps expects to calculate severity/priority in ServiceNow.

risks.title: Production go-live before Event Management configuration and plugins are stable
risks.description: Event rules, respond rules, CI binding logic, and some plugins/scheduled jobs in upper environments are still under active revision. Doug has had to rebuild event rules from scratch due to conflicting behaviors, and some plugins in cloned environments require repair. There is pressure to meet the April 1, 2026 go‑live date for AIOps Event Management.

risks.title: Event forwarding between ServiceNow production and lower environments will function for test data
risks.description: The team is planning to use ServiceNow’s event forwarding from the production instance to dev and QA so that lower environments receive representative Datadog event traffic for testing rules and correlation without needing separate Datadog integrations for each environment.

risks.title: Delayed monitor and tag standardization for GTM4 and SIAM may slip AIOps onboarding timelines
risks.description: GTM4 and SIAM subject-matter experts have expressed concerns that they may not be able to complete required Datadog monitor/tag standardization work (FinOpsDatadogAlerts updates, Asset Insight ID, primary support group, TR API name tags) by the targeted dates (end of this week / May 18). Luis has begun making some standardization changes, but key inputs such as synthetic monitor design and TR API name still depend on product teams. Without those updates, the AIOps webhook cannot be enabled because payloads would lack required fields, preventing correct grouping, routing, and service identification for these products.

risks.title: Missing Service Associations in AIOps-generated incidents may delay Datadog cutover
risks.description: Legal Tracker incidents created via AIOps in ServiceNow are missing service associations (impacted service mappings) or have them populated incorrectly. As of 12-May, this is called out as an LT blocker and work-in-progress item owned by Doug, with the project explicitly stating that Datadog direct incident creation cannot be cut off until the service association issue is resolved.

risks.title: FedRAMP governance and plugin enablement may constrain or delay AIOps usage in regulated environments
risks.description: For FedRAMP, the team must complete governance and compliance documentation (a spreadsheet demonstrating controls and processes) and has opted in to all relevant ServiceNow plugins ahead of a platform clone over the weekend. Tim expects no significant change impact, but until the documentation is accepted and post-clone behaviour is validated, there is residual uncertainty about whether FedRAMP requirements or plugin changes could constrain or delay use of AIOps integrations in regulated environments.

risks.title: Lack of standardized Datadog monitor configuration and observability governance may hinder AIOps rollout
risks.description: Datadog monitors across Thomson Reuters are owned by many different teams without a single centralized observability practice. Priority, severity, tags, and other configuration standards are inconsistently applied, and many monitors are configured primarily for escalation convenience (e.g., over‑using P1/P2).

risks.title: Single-occurrence Datadog alerts remaining as orphan alerts without incidents
risks.description: ServiceNow AIOps is currently configured so that incidents are only created after grouping multiple alerts. During the 11 May 2026 sync, Luis noted that some alerts are left as 'orphans' because they only occur once and therefore never become part of a multi-alert group that triggers incident creation. Until expectations are clarified with the Legal Tracker team and configuration is adjusted, there is a risk that valid single-occurrence alerts will not generate incidents, reducing visibility into certain issues.

risks.title: Out-of-the-box event and alert rules may not cover all Legal Tracker scenarios
risks.description: The team intends to start with mostly out‑of‑the‑box ServiceNow event rules and a very small number of TR‑specific rules (around three). Some known scenarios, such as monitors triggering on multiple hosts, are not fully addressed yet and cause sub‑optimal grouping.

risks.title: No clear ownership and governance model for Event Management could recreate Datadog ‘mess’
risks.description: There is currently no formally established owner for ServiceNow Event Management and AIOps governance; without this, different teams may create and modify rules, payloads, and processes inconsistently, similar to the fragmented situation in Datadog today.

risks.title: Poor KB/runbook quality limiting AI-driven remediation and playbooks
risks.description: Existing knowledge base articles and runbooks are fragmented, often stored in Azure DevOps wikis, and of uneven quality. The project intends to use ServiceNow AIOps (LEAP, Now Assist) and playbooks for automated or assisted remediation, which depend heavily on reliable KB content and standardized runbooks.

risks.title: Datadog → ServiceNow production connectivity may not be working at go‑live
risks.description: OAuth / webhook connectivity from Datadog production to the ServiceNow production event table may fail (401 errors or authorization issues), preventing events from being ingested when the webhook endpoint is cut over to production.

risks.title: Insufficient Legal Tracker event volume for tuning event rules and correlation
risks.description: Current Legal Tracker monitors are only sending a small number of events (e.g., 40–50) into the ServiceNow dev event table, far below the true number of monitors (~900+). This provides too little variety and volume to reliably design and test event rules, alert grouping, and CI binding before go‑live.

risks.title: Machine-learning-based alert grouping may incorrectly group unrelated alerts and erode trust in AIOps
risks.description: ServiceNow’s machine-learning-based alert grouping is currently grouping unrelated alerts (e.g., a synthetic and an infrastructure monitor) into a single group for Legal Tracker, apparently based on CI relationships. Andrea and Luis observed at least one recent example where the impacted services differed but the alerts were still grouped, and Luis confirmed this grouping did not come from the TR-defined rules but from ServiceNow’s ML logic. If ML continues to group unrelated alerts, Legal Tracker and GCC will not be able to rely on alert groups to understand issues, and teams may push to disable AI features entirely, undermining the value of AIOps.

risks.title: Loss of AIOps program lead may impact configuration and governance continuity
risks.description: Chris Rutherford, the ServiceNow / Platform Engineering leader and de facto program lead for the SNOW AIOps implementation, is leaving the project as of the end of April 2026. Chris has been a key architect for event management design, incident priority behaviour, and governance decisions. His departure may slow decision-making on rule changes, governance models, and onboarding patterns for new products, especially while Legal Tracker is still stabilising and additional products are preparing to onboard.

risks.title: ServiceNow CIservice association behaviour may block cutover from Datadog incidents
risks.description: During the May 12, 2026 AIOps Product Onboarding regional sync, the team observed that ServiceNow is not associating services with the correct CIs for large applications such as Legal Tracker. Internal analysis suggests that a configurable limit of approximately 1,000 CIs per service causes additional CIs to be handled via dynamic CI groups, which in turn prevents correct service association and grouping. ServiceNows consultant (Doug) indicated there are traverse rules that might address this but needs to consult CMDB experts. Until a clear recommendation and fix are in place, the Legal Tracker product team considers this a showstopper for disabling Datadog-direct incident creation.

risks.title: Legal Tracker AIOps implementation fails to deliver incident reduction and customer value
risks.description: Despite Legal Tracker being the pilot product, AIOps/Event Management is not yet delivering the expected reduction in incidents or operational value. As of the April 21, 2026 lessons-learned session, Legal Tracker remains on a 1:1 Datadog alert-to-incident model in production, grouping rules have recently been configured in a way that adds little value (e.g., grouping by Asset Insight ID only), critical data prerequisites (Datadog tags, assignment groups, CMDB CI state) are still being remediated, and clear success criteria and ownership for rule maintenance are only now being defined. If this continues, the Legal Tracker team may not adopt Event Management as a new way of working, and the pilot will not demonstrate the promised benefits for broader rollout.

risks.title: Machine learning-based 'group text' alert grouping may incorrectly combine or misclassify alerts
risks.description: ServiceNow AIOps is applying machine learning ('group text' type) to group alerts based on similarities in alert descriptions. For Legal Tracker, many alert descriptions share similar text patterns, which has led to at least one case where unrelated alerts were grouped together unexpectedly. Because the ML model is tuned on existing data and technical teams are only now learning how to adjust its behaviour, there is a risk that machine learning-based groupings will over-group or mis-group alerts before the configuration and operating model are fully established.

risks.title: Duplicate or inflated incident volumes during AIOps and Datadog parallel run
risks.description: When AIOps/Event Management starts creating incidents from alerts while the existing direct Datadog→ServiceNow incident integration is still active, the same underlying issues may result in multiple incidents or an increased incident count during the transition period.

risks.title: Delayed and non-compliant enablement of AIOps/Event Management in FedRAMP environment
risks.description: During the 11 May 2026 sync, AD asked about enabling AIOps/Event Management in the FedRAMP environment for high-noise FedRAMP applications (including HighQ). Tim Roe confirmed that no AIOps/Event Management work has yet started in FedRAMP and that an assessment is required to mirror enterprise configuration while complying with FedRAMP processes, approvals, and licensing constraints. There is also a need to ensure AI-related configurations (such as do not share data for AI training) are correctly set, as in the enterprise instance.

risks.title: ServiceNow event forwarding limits may cause loss of forwarded events for Datadog-based testing
risks.description: ServiceNow event forwarding from production to lower environments (dev/QA) is configured with both a daily limit and a one-hour time window. HiCase feedback from ServiceNow Support indicates that forwarding does not backfill historical events and respects these limits. During the 30-Apr-2026 regular sync, Yash highlighted that this combination introduces a risk that some Datadog events will not be forwarded (for example, older events outside the one-hour duration or when daily forwarding thresholds are reached), which could lead to missing test data in dev/QA or incomplete visibility if forwarding is used operationally.

risks.title: Unvalidated Legal Tracker incident compression metrics may misrepresent AIOps benefits and hide missed incidents
risks.description: On 1-June-2026, Mike Krause presented preliminary Power BI analysis showing that average Legal Tracker incident volume appears to have dropped from ~91 incidents/day (1–19 May) to ~9 incidents/day (21–31 May) after Datadog-direct incident creation was commented out and Event Management incidents became the primary source. However, Mike and Paul Berry noted that these figures are currently anecdotal and depend on ad-hoc filters (e.g., treating incidents opened by "system administrator" as AIOps and by the Datadog service account as legacy) and on payload fields that the existing report does not yet parse (including some blank or differently shaped monitor IDs). There has been no systematic line-by-line validation to confirm that the 10x apparent compression accurately reflects duplicate/noise reduction without missing unique incidents.

risks.title: High-noise CPU utilisation monitors may hide capacity issues and distort AIOps behaviour
risks.description: Certain CPU utilisation monitors (e.g., "CPU is high on host" patterns) are generating very high alert volumes in Datadog and are frequently muted by product teams. In the 3-Jun-2026 sync, Legal Tracker examples showed warning-level CPU alerts that could indicate capacity problems but are either overly sensitive or routinely suppressed. These noisy monitors are candidates for both Datadog hygiene remediation and AIOps correlation tuning.

risks.title: Machine-learning-based AIOps grouping may incorrectly group unrelated Legal Tracker alerts
risks.description: ServiceNow AIOps machine-learning (ML)-driven alert grouping is combining unrelated Legal Tracker alerts (e.g., synthetic monitors and infrastructure monitors) into the same group based on text similarity and inferred CI relationships, even when impacted services differ. This behaviour is not controlled by Thomson Reuters’ explicit correlation rules and has already led to important infrastructure alerts being ‘hidden’ inside groups dominated by synthetic alerts.

risks.title: Insufficient CI/CMDB data quality and CI–service association may block broader onboarding despite ongoing remediation
risks.description: During the 28-May-2026 AIOps Product Onboarding regional sync, the team reconfirmed that unresolved CMDB health and CI–service association behaviour remain a gating factor for Legal Tracker and all downstream product onboardings. Subsequent working sessions (including the 8-June-2026 AIOps/Event Management regular sync) have shown that these issues also affect new early-adopter products such as ONESOURCE GTM4 and SIAM: many GTM4 configuration items referenced in Datadog alerts do not exist in the CMDB, and SIAM monitors are not linked to configuration items at all, forcing temporary workarounds (e.g., using the application as both configuration item and impacted service). Until a scalable CMDB remediation approach is implemented, applications will continue to have incomplete or incorrect CI and service mappings, limiting safe AIOps onboarding and cutover from legacy incident flows.

risks.title: Complex and inconsistent Datadog tagging standards may hinder adoption and correlation quality
risks.description: Current Datadog tagging standards and practices are complex and inconsistently applied across products. The Thomson Reuters tagging standards document defines many “required” tags (including multiple environment-related tags such as TR_environment_type, TR_environment_name, and nt_environment), but in practice product teams use different subsets and values, and many monitors have duplicate or conflicting tags (e.g., multiple environment tags on a single monitor, duplicate Asset Insight ID tags). During the 8-June-2026 AIOps/Event Management regular sync, Dominique and Mike highlighted that the environment tagging standards in the AIOps programme (e.g., TR_environment_type) differ from Datadog’s native ENV tag and that existing monitors already use ENV extensively. This complexity risks confusion and low compliance for new AIOps onboardings and undermines correlation rules that rely on specific TR_ tags.

risks.title: ServiceNow incident reopen behaviour and incident number changes may cause confusion and reporting issues
risks.description: ServiceNow Event Management is currently configured so that when a new alert group matches a previously closed incident, the platform reopens that incident and, in some observed cases, changes the incident number and unlinks/links alerts between incidents. This is out-of-the-box behaviour tied to alert grouping windows and incident-respond rules, but it is unfamiliar to Legal Tracker and GCC teams, who are used to static incident numbers and non-reopened incidents from the legacy Datadog→incident flow. The team considers the current deterministic incident-priority patch and this reopen behaviour an MVP to allow Legal Tracker to proceed, but has not yet decided whether this should become the long-term standard.

risks.title: ServiceNow Zurich upgrade mid-May may constrain configuration changes and delay permanent fixes
risks.description: A ServiceNow Zurich upgrade is scheduled to start around mid-May (approx. May 16–17). Jot noted that there may be restrictions on what configuration changes can be made during this upgrade window, which coincides with ongoing work to stabilise incident priority behaviour, CI binding, and incident reopen behaviour for Legal Tracker.

risks.title: ServiceNow incident reopen and incident number change behaviour may confuse teams and distort reporting
risks.description: In the current AIOps/Event Management configuration, ServiceNow may reopen closed incidents and, in some cases, change the incident number when new alerts are grouped into existing alert groups. Legal Tracker stakeholders (Elizabeth and Andrea, via feedback to Luis Jorge) have observed that grouped alerts can reopen a previously closed incident and that the related incident number can change when alert links are updated. This behaviour is driven by default ServiceNow grouping and respond rules (e.g., 30-minute grouping window and incident creation on alert-group creation) and is not aligned with the team’s existing ways of working or reporting expectations.

risks.title: Onboarding products without monitors-as-code or bulk-update capability may delay rollout
risks.description: During the discussion, Elizabeth highlighted that Legal Tracker’s Datadog monitors are managed as code (Terraform/GitHub), which makes it easier to apply standardized changes (tags, priorities, handlers). Chris and Jot noted that effort estimates will differ for teams that do not manage monitors as code. Luis mentioned GCC has scripts to perform bulk operations against Datadog monitors but indicated this is a workaround and not the best long‑term approach. If new products lack monitors‑as‑code or bulk‑update capabilities, onboarding them to AIOps will require more manual changes per monitor (e.g., adding handlers, tags, correcting priorities), which could slow the rollout or result in inconsistent configurations.

risks.title: Reliance on temporary customizations for incident priority and CI binding instead of AIOps-native behaviour
risks.description: To meet Legal Tracker timelines, the team has implemented temporary workarounds: (1) disabling out-of-the-box ServiceNow incident priority calculation and deterministically passing Datadog monitor priority straight through to incident priority; and (2) implementing temporary CI matching logic so that CI binding appears to work, even though underlying discovery/CMDB issues are unresolved. These changes diverge from ServiceNow AIOps standard design and are intended as MVP patches.

risks.title: Event taxonomy for informational/warning/exception states may not be defined in time for Legal Tracker
risks.description: The target-state design depends on a clear event taxonomy that distinguishes informational, warning, and exception conditions so that ServiceNow Event Management can filter, classify, and prioritize events correctly. The Target Future State deck explicitly calls out that "Event taxonomy must be defined" as a dependency for filtering and classification rules. If this taxonomy is not defined and agreed before enabling broader AIOps behaviour for Legal Tracker, filtering and prioritization rules will be based on ad-hoc or inconsistent interpretations of monitor states.

risks.title: Recurring mis-mapping of Datadog P3 alerts to critical severity/P1 incidents in ServiceNow production
risks.description: During the 24-Apr-2026 AIOps Event Management regular sync, the team confirmed that alerts coming from Datadog with P3 priority are being created in ServiceNow as critical severity, which then drives P1 incident creation. Doug identified that the custom Datadog-to-Severity event field mapping script that worked in dev is not behaving correctly in production, likely due to rule ordering and interaction with other event mappings (e.g., synthetics). Until this is fixed, enabling automatic incident creation from alerts would generate a large number of false P1 incidents.

risks.title: Parallel onboarding of GTM4 and SIAM may overextend capacity and delay effective onboarding
risks.description: The team plans to onboard both ONESOURCE GTM4 and SIAM in parallel as the next AIOps adopters. During the 11 May 2026 sync, Mike Krause raised concern that GTM4 generates a high volume of alerts and will likely produce many findings and follow-up work. Although he is not opposed to onboarding two products in parallel, he is conscious that resource and attention demands could be significant, particularly while the team is still resolving early issues from the Legal Tracker pilot.

risks.title: Insufficient CI/CMDB data quality and CI binding for effective correlation and routing
risks.description: Many incoming events lack reliable CI bindings due to inconsistent or missing metadata, such as FQDNs for Azure VMs, host/node field gaps, and inconsistent tag usage. CI mapping is often at service level only, and HighQ and other products rely heavily on tags and Asset Insight IDs. If CI binding issues are not resolved, correlation, grouping, and routing in ServiceNow will be inaccurate.

risks.title: Insufficient AIOps engineering capacity and access to scale onboarding to multiple applications
risks.description: Current AIOps onboarding and configuration work for Legal Tracker, ONESOURCE GTM4 and SIAM is heavily dependent on a single engineer (Rodriguez, Luis Jorge). During the 26-May-2026 AIOps Product Onboarding regular sync, Talia and Jot highlighted that scaling to 5–6 applications per month or per week is unrealistic with the existing capacity, even before addressing CMDB issues. Although additional engineers (e.g., Vijay, Mahesha, Owen, Erikipaty) have been identified as potential contributors, they do not yet have Event Management admin access in ServiceNow, and their roles and responsibilities in the AIOps program are not fully defined. Without increased and properly permissioned engineering capacity, onboarding timelines for the FY 2026 roadmap will slip and the program will not be able to meet leadership expectations for scale.

risks.title: Machine-learning-based alert grouping may incorrectly group unrelated Legal Tracker alerts
risks.description: ServiceNow AIOps machine-learning (ML)–driven alert grouping is combining unrelated Legal Tracker alerts (e.g., a synthetic monitor and an infrastructure monitor) into the same alert group based on CI relationships, even when impacted services differ. These ML-created groups are not using the TR-defined correlation rules. If ML continues to group dissimilar alerts, incidents derived from these groups may represent multiple distinct issues, and teams will see inconsistent, hard-to-explain behaviour in Event Management.

risks.title: ServiceNow event forwarding limits may cause loss of events in lower environments
risks.description: ServiceNow event forwarding from production to lower environments (dev/QA) appears subject to a per-day forwarding limit and a one-hour event duration window. Yash raised a concern that, under the current configuration, older events outside the one-hour window may not be forwarded, creating a risk that some Datadog-originating events will never reach dev/QA for rule testing and correlation validation.

risks.title: Incident creation policy and notification tiers may not be agreed before event-first processing is enabled
risks.description: The Target Future State and capability prioritization highlight open design decisions around incident creation policy (which events should create incidents vs remain as events or trigger auto-remediation) and notification tiers (what severity warrants after-hours paging vs next-business-day notification). These are listed as later-phase design items, yet the routing and resolution stages of the target lifecycle depend on them. If incident creation policy and notification tiers are not agreed before enabling broader event-first processing for Legal Tracker, incidents and on-call pages may not reflect true business impact.

risks.title: Insufficient CI/CMDB data quality and CI/service association may block broader onboarding despite ongoing remediation
risks.description: During the 28-May-2026 AIOps Product Onboarding regional sync, the team reconfirmed that unresolved CMDB health and CIservice association behaviour remain a gating factor for Legal Tracker and all downstream product onboardings. Talia reiterated that the new ServiceNow resource (Bill) has proposed an approach to address the CI/service association problem (including the current configurable ~1,000-CI-per-service parameter and overall service mapping strategy), and that a detailed pre-read and action plan are expected for the 4-June session. AD and Eric explicitly questioned whether the magnitude of the CMDB problem is being underestimated and noted that if the CI/service association issue is not understood and fixed, it will halt implementation for additional applications and jeopardize the September onboarding roadmap. Jot highlighted that any approach which relies on application teams to validate and reduce their CI sets could introduce significant lift and delay, because most teams lack mature documentation and would need to manually validate which CIs are actually consumed by their processes. The team agreed that CMDB health and service mapping must become an explicit prerequisite and part of the onboarding process for each application, and that the feasibility of the multimonth roadmap depends directly on the outcome of Bills design and the CMDB teams capacity to execute it.

actions.title: Define and document support model for Legal Tracker post-AIOps go-live
actions.description: Prepare a clear support model for Legal Tracker once AIOps/Event Management is live in production, including who the product team should contact for issues, how to raise support requests, and verification that the team has appropriate access to Event Management and related workspaces.

actions.title: Investigate ML-based alert grouping anomaly with ServiceNow consultant Doug
actions.description: Review the Legal Tracker alert group where a synthetic and an infrastructure monitor were incorrectly grouped together. Confirm whether ServiceNow machine learning–based grouping is still active, analyze why these alerts were grouped via CI relationships despite different impacted services, and agree changes with Doug so that future groupings follow the agreed TR rules only.

actions.title: Validate CI binding behaviour for Legal Tracker after discovery fixes
actions.description: Perform sample validation of CI binding for Legal Tracker events in ServiceNow following the discovery fixes implemented by Kolluru, Prudhvi Yaswanth, to confirm that CI binding now works as expected before involving the Legal Tracker product team.

actions.title: Support Tim with code changes for incident priority mapping in dev

issues.title: ServiceNow CI binding not working as expected for Legal Tracker events
issues.description: Events ingested from Datadog into ServiceNow are not automatically associating to existing CIs in the CMDB, even when matching CI names exist, causing CI binding to fail for many events.

issues.title: Potential duplicate/incidental increase during AIOps cutover
issues.description: Enabling AIOps‑driven incident creation while leaving existing Datadog→ServiceNow incident integrations active could temporarily increase incident counts or create near‑duplicate incidents until Datadog incident creation is disabled.

issues.title: AIOps-generated incidents breaching response SLA due to closure before acknowledgement
issues.description: Legal Tracker incidents created via the AIOps/Event Management pipeline are sometimes being resolved/closed without an acknowledgement step, leading to response SLA breaches even though the incidents are ultimately resolved. Andrea observed that incidents show as resolved but still appear as having breached SLA, and Luis suspects the response SLA is breaking because incidents are being closed before acknowledgement.

issues.title: ServiceNow event forwarding limits may drop older events during lower-environment testing
issues.description: ServiceNow event forwarding from production to lower environments operates with a per-day forwarding limit and a one-hour duration window, and does not backfill historical events. As confirmed in the ServiceNow Support HiCase reviewed on 30-Apr-2026, this behaviour risks losing events older than one hour and may prevent complete event streams from being forwarded to dev/QA for AIOps rule testing.

issues.title: ServiceNow AIOps machine learning grouping is combining unrelated Legal Tracker alerts
issues.description: ServiceNow AIOps machine learning is grouping Legal Tracker alerts that should not be grouped together (e.g., a synthetic monitor alert and an infrastructure monitor alert with different impacted services). These ML-created groups bypass the Thomson Reuters–defined correlation rules, causing inconsistent alert grouping behaviour for Legal Tracker.

issues.title: GCC lacks access to ServiceNow Event Management for Legal Tracker alerts
issues.description: The GCC manager for Legal Tracker (Rajendran Van) and GCC analysts do not currently have access to the ServiceNow Event Management module and cannot see or work with Legal Tracker alert groups. Only Rodriguez, Luis Jorge is currently reviewing alerts in Event Management for Legal Tracker.

issues.title: Missing or incorrect service associations in AIOps-generated incidents for Legal Tracker
issues.description: Incidents created through the ServiceNow AIOps/Event Management pipeline for Legal Tracker are missing or incorrectly populated service associations (impacted service fields). As a temporary workaround, incident priority and service are being passed directly from Datadog monitors, but a long-term, platform-native fix for impacted service mapping is still being designed and implemented.

issues.title: Confusing incident reopen behaviour and incident number changes for AIOps-generated incidents
issues.description: For Legal Tracker, incidents created via the ServiceNow AIOps/Event Management pipeline are being reopened when new alert groups arrive and, in some cases, the incident number changes and related alerts are unlinked from prior incidents. This behaviour is confusing Legal Tracker stakeholders and may impact historical tracking and reporting.

issues.title: CI binding now working but CI–service association limits remain a concern
issues.description: Following recent discovery and CI-binding fixes by Kolluru, Prudhvi Yaswanth, CI binding for Legal Tracker assets is expected to work as intended (no active VMs in retired state, discovery failures remediated, and custom logic deactivated). However, a ServiceNow limitation on the number of CI associations per application service (around 1,000 CIs) may still prevent correct service association for large applications using tag-based service mappings.

issues.title: ServiceNow AIOps machine learning text-based grouping continues to incorrectly combine Legal Tracker alerts, causing operational impact
issues.description: ServiceNows text-based machine-learning alert grouping is still grouping unrelated Legal Tracker alerts into a single alert group based on similarities in alert descriptions and titles, even when the alerts come from different monitor types (e.g., synthetics vs disk/CPU infrastructure) and have different impacted services. In at least one recent case, a disk-usage alert was grouped under a synthetic primary alert, causing the disk issue to be effectively hidden within the group and contributing to a major situation for Legal Tracker.

issues.title: Inconsistent alert grouping for Legal Tracker due to AI/ML-based CI relationship grouping
issues.description: ServiceNows machine-learning-based event correlation is grouping unrelated Legal Tracker alerts into a single alert group based on inferred CI relationships, including combining a synthetic monitor alert and an infrastructure monitor alert even when impacted services differ. These ML-created groups are not aligned with the TR-defined correlation rules agreed for Legal Tracker.

issues.title: Incident reopening and incident number changes for AIOps-generated incidents
issues.description: For Legal Tracker, incidents created via the ServiceNow AIOps/Event Management pipeline are being reopened and, in some cases, assigned new incident numbers when additional alerts are grouped into an existing alert group. Related alerts are being unlinked from previous incidents and attached to new ones, causing confusion for operators and complicating historical tracking and reporting.

issues.title: CI binding and CI–service association still failing for Legal Tracker after attempted fixes
issues.description: Despite earlier statements that discovery issues were fixed and CI binding should now work, sample checks during the April 30, 2026 AIOps Product Onboarding regional sync showed that recent Legal Tracker alerts in ServiceNow are still missing CI bindings and/or are associated to incorrect services. A suspected ServiceNow product limitation (approximately 1,000 CIs per service) and incomplete follow-up with ServiceNow and internal platform teams are contributing factors.

issues.title: GCC team lacks access to ServiceNow Event Management for Legal Tracker alerts
issues.description: The GCC manager for Legal Tracker (Rajendran Van) and GCC operators do not currently have access to the ServiceNow Event Management workspace, so they cannot see or work Legal Tracker alerts created by AIOps. Luis has explained the application behaviour to GCC, but access has not yet been provisioned.

issues.title: AIOps-generated incident priorities are higher than corresponding alert priorities
issues.description: Incidents created by ServiceNow AIOps from group alerts are being assigned higher priorities (often P1) than expected based on the underlying alert severity and priority. Analysis of the 'create incident TR presets' subflow and related flow actions shows that incident impact and urgency are set to their highest values whenever the alert priority group or severity is 1 or 2, which forces the incident priority matrix to produce P1 incidents. In addition, the alert 'priority group' field is driven by an out-of-the-box priority score that may not align with Thomson Reuters expectations, and current event rules map Datadog monitor priority into alert severity but do not explicitly map priority into the alert priority group. As a result, Legal Tracker alerts with moderate priorities (e.g., P3) can still generate P1 incidents, causing misaligned incident priorities compared to direct Datadog-created incidents.

issues.title: Datadog P3 alerts mapped as critical severity in ServiceNow alerts for Legal Tracker
issues.description: In the ServiceNow production instance, Legal Tracker alerts coming from Datadog with monitor priority P3 are being mapped to critical severity on the ServiceNow alert records. As a result, incidents created from these alerts appear as P1, even though the underlying Datadog monitors are configured as P3. The problem appears to originate in the custom ServiceNow event field mapping rule "Datadog map alert priority to severity" not behaving as it did in dev, potentially due to rule ordering or execution context.

issues.title: Datadog to ServiceNow production OAuth authentication failures (401 errors)
issues.description: After pointing the Datadog webhook to the ServiceNow production instance, Datadog receives HTTP 401 responses when attempting to send events, indicating authentication/authorization failures.

issues.title: ServiceNow AIOps machine-learning grouping combining unrelated Legal Tracker alerts
issues.description: ServiceNow AIOps machine-learning–driven alert grouping is combining unrelated Legal Tracker alerts (e.g., synthetic and infrastructure monitors with different impacted services) into the same alert group based on CI relationships, instead of following Thomson Reuters–defined correlation rules.

RevTech Focus Area: Commercial Model Simplification

risks.title: Unclear PROS‑to‑EPM price publishing process may delay Release 2 price management readiness
risks.description: For products whose price lists are managed in EPM strategic stacks (e.g., Pagero), the end‑to‑end process for publishing PROS‑generated prices into EPM—including approvals, data structures, and automation boundaries—has not yet been fully defined. This clarity is required to support Release 2 price management capabilities.

risks.title: Customer data source for pricing may not contain complete parent–child hierarchy
risks.description: The program is moving towards using GSI as the customer data source for pricing. However, there was uncertainty whether GSI contains the required parent–child customer relationships (e.g., global vs regional accounts) needed for pricing logic, and whether those relationships from ECM/D&B are properly propagated to GSI.

risks.title: Price list structure and pricing model design may not be agreed in time for Release 2 price management
risks.description: The program still needs to align on the number of price lists, their segmentation logic (e.g., by product line, business unit, or sub-business unit), and the pricing models/formulas that will be configured in PROS. Current discussions reference SAP granularity (customer group, material ID, sales org, UOM), but there is not yet consensus on how to partition price books in PROS or how many price lists will exist. Neetika highlighted this as one of the most important design decisions for price management that needs to be closed within about a week and before the April 17 design target.

risks.title: Pricing engine call latency due to Boomi processing and batch design
risks.description: End‑to‑end pricing and optimization calls from Conga through Boomi to PROS may exceed acceptable response times, particularly during high‑volume transactions. This risk exists because Boomi parallel processing and batching patterns are being implemented for this use case for the first time, PROS batch size limits and throughput are still being validated, and final performance SLAs have not yet been proven under realistic load conditions. There is also uncertainty whether additional Boomi infrastructure capacity or PROS license scaling will be required to meet target response times.

risks.title: Fragmented intake requests may disrupt Release 1 design closure and SLA alignment
risks.description: New intake requests related to Pricing Engine Release 1 (e.g., SAP, EPM, data, integrations) may be submitted without explicit linkage to the original program‑level intake, causing the work to be treated as net‑new. This can reset SLA expectations, create prioritization misalignment, and introduce confusion around scope, ownership, and delivery timelines during Release 1 design activities.

risks.title: PROS REST API delay and server errors may block Release 1 and Release 2 integration timelines
risks.description: Server errors in RTPE (Real-Time Pricing Engine) calls were root-caused to product description/code mismatches and data quality issues in the TR extract. Although a corrected extract was delivered on 2026-05-26, PROS has not yet fully reloaded and validated RTPE. In parallel, delivery of the PROS REST API (final request/response mappings and endpoint) is delayed, with RAID 1281891 raised to track this. Boomi development is blocked on receiving the final API version and payloads, and Release 1 and Release 2 timelines are at risk until the PROS API is available and stable.

risks.title: Integration layer complexity due to XML-only PROS output may delay EPM price ingestion and increase Boomi scope
risks.description: An Architecture Call confirmed that PROS can output only XML and that CSV exports cannot include approvals. The agreed PROS–EPM integration pattern is PROS → Middleware → EPM in CSV format, with Day-1 manual operations and Day-2 automation. To support this, middleware must now perform XML-to-CSV conversion and transform delta updates from PROS into full-snapshot CSV files for EPM. This expands the integration layer scope beyond the originally envisioned Boomi mapping work and introduces new design and build effort that is not yet fully estimated.

risks.title: Delay in business validation of data mappings may impact Release 1 ETL and Go Live readiness
risks.description: Business validation of data mappings across key entities (customer, product, transactional quote/order data, and asset/contract data) is still in progress. While foundational design is complete, delayed validation of remaining attributes and business logic may slow ETL development, data loads into PROS, and integration testing required for Release 1 Go Live.

risks.title: Delay in receiving transactional order data extracts for price optimization design
risks.description: The team is unable to pull historical transactional/orders data from at least one source system and is also dependent on the MDM team to deliver a full extract of active materials and transactional variations across in-scope products. This data is required to understand how many variations exist (e.g., multiple UOM, banded vs fixed pricing) and to design how the price optimization engine and business rules will differentiate between models.

risks.title: Adding Mid Law testing alongside Small Law in Release 1 may strain UAT scope and timelines
risks.description: Originally, Release 1 UAT was aligned to focus on Small Law. Recent discussions with business teams indicate that Mid Law also wants to start testing in parallel with Small Law, using largely overlapping use cases but with some Mid Law–specific scenarios (including approval dashboard requirements). Yogesh confirmed that Small Law and Mid Law testing can happen in parallel, with weekly working sessions (Tuesdays and Thursdays), but enablement timing for Mid Law in production is still to be decided by the pricing/business team. Anantha noted this as a change item that needs leadership awareness and sign‑off, and there is not yet a clear, documented plan for when Mid Law will be enabled relative to Small Law.

risks.title: Data readiness risk: incomplete guidance and analytics data may delay next sprint stories
risks.description: As of Week 20, Release 1 optimization data is only partially complete: approximately 50 attributes have been shared with PROS and fees generation is still in progress. Analytics data needed for UDD dashboard charts (e.g., ACV%, discount%) is not yet fully available. This partial data set blocks certain next-sprint stories that depend on complete guidance and analytics inputs.

risks.title: Sprint spillover risk: R1 and R2 stories may carry over and compress timelines
risks.description: Week 20 status indicates that for Release 1 (price optimization) approximately 4–6 stories are expected to spill over from Sprint 4, and for Release 2 (price management and analytics) approximately 7–8 stories are expected to spill over from Sprint 2. This cumulative spillover of around 12 stories may compress subsequent sprints and testing windows.

risks.title: Risk of exceeding PROS usage limits by onboarding all tenants
risks.description: Current direction was to onboard PROS for all tenants, but concerns were raised that if all tenants invoke PROS, the number of calls could quickly reach or exceed licensed or technically supported limits.

risks.title: Limits in SAP/EPM geographic granularity may constrain Release 2 pricing strategy
risks.description: The strategic pricing program has requested location‑specific list prices (e.g., state‑level pricing within a country). While PROS can model geography as a pricing dimension, it is not yet confirmed whether SAP and EPM master data and pricing models can support and operationalize this level of geographic granularity at scale. This clarification is required as part of Release 2 price management design.

risks.title: Key design decisions (KDDs) for price management and analytics may not be closed by April 17
risks.description: Design sessions for Release 2 price management and pricing analytics have started, but the team is still in the familiarization phase and there are multiple key design decisions (KDDs) outstanding. Neetika stated that these KDDs are being targeted to close by April 17, and additional workshops are being scheduled up to that date. Given the volume of open questions (including price list structures, analytics requirements, and dashboard/chart constraints), there is a risk that not all KDDs will be fully resolved in time.

risks.title: Dual‑UAT testing approach may increase effort and impact Release 1 test timelines
risks.description: Managing testing across two UAT environments may require duplicate execution of test scenarios, increasing effort and coordination complexity. This could delay UAT completion, introduce test coverage gaps, and negatively impact Release 1 Go‑Live readiness if not tightly planned and managed.

risks.title: JWT-only PROS–TR integration approach may be delayed or rejected by Architecture Review Board
risks.description: The connection between the PROS environment and Thomson Reuters (TR) environment is currently designed to use a JWT token–based integration from Boomi to PROS. PROS product team confirmed that JWT is the only supported option (no OAuth or other alternatives). The proposed JWT solution is working in initial trials, but it still requires formal approval from the architectural review board (IRS/architecture forum), where the Boomi architect will present the design. Until this approval is granted, the integration pattern remains at risk of change.

risks.title: Release 1 data extract delays increasing likelihood of late price optimization design and testing
risks.description: Week 18–19 status reports that Release 1 is trending Red due to incomplete data extracts required by PROS to progress sprint work, including pending derived attributes for optimization. This amplifies the existing concern that historical transactional/order data and related attributes will not be available in time to support price optimization design, rule configuration, and testing.

risks.title: Order Capture event‑type alignment may block Sprint 4 Release 1 optimization configuration
risks.description: Release 1 Sprint 4 depends on confirming the event-type model in Order Capture so that price optimization business rules can be correctly triggered and evaluated. As of the Week 18–19 status, event-type confirmation is described as the primary remaining gating item for Release 1 optimization outcomes. Until event types are finalized and aligned across Order Capture, Conga, Boomi, and PROS, the team cannot fully configure or validate optimization rules, risking further sprint spillover and delays in producing raw guidance.

risks.title: Order Capture event-type alignment may block Sprint 4 Release 1 optimization configuration
risks.description: Release 1 Sprint 4 depends on confirming the event-type model in Order Capture so that price optimization business rules can be correctly triggered and evaluated. As of the Week 18–19 status, event-type confirmation is described as the primary remaining gating item for Release 1 optimization outcomes. Until event types are finalized and aligned across Order Capture, Conga, Boomi, and PROS, the team cannot fully configure or validate optimization rules, risking further sprint spillover and delays in producing raw guidance.

risks.title: Unresolved PROS–SAP price list mechanism and analytics data granularity may cause Release 2 sprint spillover
risks.description: In Week 18–19 status, Release 2 is in Sprint 2 with development focused on analytics setup and sample data loads. Progress is constrained by unresolved integration and design questions, specifically the mechanism for sending price lists from PROS to SAP (e.g., XML vs CSV) and alignment on analytics data granularity. These open items gate completion of Sprint 2 stories and threaten to cause sprint spillover and delay downstream work, even though development capacity itself is not the bottleneck.

risks.title: Integration design risk: Conga–Boomi field name alignment may miss May 27 design deadline
risks.description: Conga–Boomi field mappings for pricing calls are still being aligned, with specific issues such as inconsistent naming (e.g., mapping between Conga’s sold-to ID and the customer identifier expected by Boomi/PROS). Although a manual end-to-end path has been confirmed and Boomi is able to send correct customer and product IDs from 2026-05-19, unresolved field name alignment and mapping design items remain, all of which must be closed by the 2026-05-27 design drop-dead date.

risks.title: External dependency risk: EPM–Semarchy migration and SAP RPA decision may impact schedule
risks.description: Week 20 highlights two external dependencies that could affect the Pricing Engine timelines: (1) the EPM–Semarchy migration, which must complete by July 2026, and (2) a SAP RPA (Robotic Process Automation) go/no-go decision, which is due by 2026-05-31. Delays or unfavorable outcomes in these dependencies may impact price list and analytics readiness or require workaround processes.

risks.title: Parent–child pricing behavior limited in Release 1, requiring manual workaround
risks.description: Architecture forums have flagged parent–child pricing as a Release 1 risk. PROS-based custom tables to drive parent–child pricing were determined to be not feasible for Release 1, and the design decision for parent–child rules has been reopened. The only viable option for Release 1 is to rely on PROS’ native capabilities and a manual one-time load of parent–child relationships, with a more robust fix deferred to Release 2.

risks.title: End-to-end pricing call performance SLA not yet agreed for Release 1
risks.description: The program does not yet have a confirmed performance model and SLA for pricing calls initiated from Conga and processed via Boomi to PROS. Boomi is implementing parallel processing with request splitting, but their current SLA is 2.5 seconds, and they cannot yet confirm expected processing time for the new pattern. Additional latency is expected due to multiple sequential calls (~3 × 300 ms), and it is unclear whether performance can be achieved without infrastructure or license cost increases. Business stakeholders have not yet agreed to the expected performance impact for initial releases.

issues.title: Release 1 development trending Red due to data and integration blockers
issues.description: Release 1 is trending Red because server errors and REST API delays on the PROS side, combined with earlier data extract issues, have constrained Sprint 11 development. Although TR Priority 1 and 2 data items have been resolved and a corrected extract (with unique IDs, add-on, AI/non-AI data) was delivered on May 26, 2026, PROS has not yet completed data reload and RTPE validation. Boomi has reduced story points this sprint due to uncertainty and dependency on PROS mappings and payloads, and 14 Release 1 stories have spilled over into the next sprint.

issues.title: Customer parent–child hierarchy source initially unclear for Pricing Engine
issues.description: At the start of the discussion, there was uncertainty about whether customer parent–child relationships (e.g., KPMG global vs. regional branches) are available in GSI or only in ECM. This hierarchy is critical for pricing scenarios requiring roll-ups to parent accounts. It was not clear if ECM/D&B-derived hierarchy data is pushed back into GSI and accessible for use in pricing.

issues.title: Unclear EPM strategic process for ingesting prices from PROS
issues.description: The process and approach for loading price lists from PROS into EPM (particularly for Pagero and strategic stack products such as Pagero and Shore Prep) is not clearly understood. Current EPM processes involve significant manual steps and multiple approvals, and there was no representation from EPM strategic or SAP teams in the prior call. The team needs to align on how PROS, as system of origin for certain price lists, will interface with EPM in both legacy and strategic contexts.

issues.title: Complex dual-UAT testing setup for Pricing Engine may increase effort and delay timelines
issues.description: To work around inaccurate data in the existing UAT environment and the inability to fully refresh UAT before late September, the team will run two separate UAT environments in parallel: (1) a fully integrated UAT environment for end-to-end flows (ECM → GSI → SAP, etc.), and (2) a dedicated production-copy UAT environment connected only to PROS for price optimization testing, where orders cannot be submitted but carts and discounts can be exercised. Business testers (including Commercial Excellence) expressed that this dual-environment approach is complex, will require double testing, and is not ideal, increasing the risk of timeline slippage.

issues.title: End‑to‑end pricing call performance SLA not yet agreed for Release 1
issues.description: The program does not yet have a confirmed performance model and SLA for pricing calls initiated from Conga and processed via Boomi to PROS. Boomi is implementing parallel processing with request splitting, but their current SLA is 2.5 seconds, and they cannot yet confirm expected processing time for the new pattern. Additional latency is expected due to multiple sequential calls (~3 × 300 ms), and it is unclear whether performance can be achieved without infrastructure or license cost increases. Business stakeholders have not yet agreed to the expected performance impact for initial releases.

issues.title: Release 1 development trending Red due to incomplete data extracts and pending attribute mappings
issues.description: Release 1 is currently in Sprint 4 and is trending Red because (1) attribute mappings are still incomplete and (2) PROS has not received a complete data extract, including derived attributes, required to progress optimization sprint work. Sprint capacity is being impacted by carryover items and active blockers, and the missing data and mappings are now directly constraining development and preventing generation of raw pricing guidance.

issues.title: PROS REST API delays and endpoint errors blocking integration (RAID 1281891)
issues.description: PROS REST API response delivery and endpoint stability are delaying Release 1 and Release 2 pricing integration. Server errors were traced to product description/code mismatches in the initial data extract; TR delivered a corrected extract on May 26, 2026, but PROS must reload and validate the Real-Time Pricing Engine (RTPE). Until PROS provides stable REST endpoints and near-final request/response payloads, Boomi cannot proceed with mapping sheet completion, error handling design, or full integration development. RAID 1281891 has been logged in ADO to track this risk/issue, and escalation has occurred up to Palani as of May 27.

entities.name: FedRAMP Authorization
entities.status: The FedRAMP Authorization program coordinates cross-functional work across Thomson Reuters technology pillars, ISRM, Product Management, Service Management, Platform Engineering, and external partners (e.g., HHS, Schellman, Fortreum) to obtain FedRAMP authorization for the TR Legal Research and TR Risk & Fraud packages. The program manages remediation of shared vulnerabilities and manual control / penetration test findings, implementation of required security controls across AWS and Azure environments, and ongoing monitoring to sustain compliance until authorization is granted and beyond.

risks.title: FedRAMP authorization may be jeopardized by unresolved container vulnerabilities across TR Legal Research and TR Risk & Fraud
risks.description: Moderate and low container vulnerabilities identified in RA-5 container scans for both Thomson Reuters Legal Research and Thomson Reuters Risk & Fraud (as submitted to Schellman on 6 November 2025) may not be reduced or managed sufficiently within FedRAMP expectations. If these vulnerabilities persist or new ones are introduced during the audit window, the sponsoring agency (HHS) or the 3PAO may consider the residual risk unacceptable, jeopardizing initial FedRAMP authorization or leading to conditions on the authorization that affect both product packages.

risks.title: Network disconnect control (SC-10) for privileged users remains as a POA&M item across FedRAMP packages

The program plans to manage this gap as a POA&M item under PMO oversight, but there is a risk that prolonged non-compliance with this control could be viewed unfavourably by HHS or the 3PAO.

risks.title: Inadequate restrictions on use of company credentials for external platforms (PL-4(1)) impacting FedRAMP compliance
risks.description: The current Thomson Reuters Code of Conduct lacks explicit restrictions on using company credentials to create accounts on external platforms, which is required under PL-4(1). This policy gap affects all staff supporting the FedRAMP environments for TR Legal Research and TR Risk & Fraud and creates a program-level compliance risk until the policy is updated and adopted.

entities.name: Legacy Product Migration
entities.status: Program to migrate multiple legacy commercial and legal product systems (including LATAM sales and Legal Tracker) from S2E, Salesforce (SFDC), and bespoke solutions to strategic enterprise platforms (GSI, ECM, EPM). The program will deliver standardized cross‑regional workflows, improved data quality and integrity, reduced technical debt, and the decommissioning of legacy technology and associated licenses within the 2026 timeframe.

risks.title: Shared SAP / EPM / integration dependencies across projects may not be delivered on time
risks.description: All three projects in the Legacy Product Migration program rely on shared SAP and EPM capabilities and integrations: Special Offers requires material master creation, TR level codes (L4/L5), and full data availability in EPM; Legal Tracker depends on ZPEND work in SAP and product/price checks in EPM; LatAm requires GSI/ECM alignment and integration. Delays or defects in these shared platform/integration components pose a program‑level risk.

risks.description: There is a risk that compensation and finance teams will push back on opening up future start functionality due to concerns that it could create opportunities for overpayments.

risks.description: Previously, a condensed QA schedule created a risk to the September enhancements for Enterprise Access and Future Starts by limiting SIT and UAT testing windows.

risks.title: Pushback from pricing on Enterprise Access due to increased material management complexity
risks.description: There is a risk that the pricing team will push back on Enterprise Access because it may require managing a larger number of materials, increasing complexity and operational workload.

risks.title: Inconsistent end‑to‑end user experience across products and regions after migration
risks.description: The program aims to standardize processes and improve user experience by moving LATAM and Legal Tracker from legacy systems (S2E, SFDC) to enterprise platforms (GSI, ECM, EPM). However, Legal Tracker’s end‑to‑end user experience is currently unknown, and LatAm is considering partial/Top‑of‑Funnel migration options while service and back‑office processes may remain on S2E. Special Offers is moving to OC/SAP/Conga. This creates a program‑level risk of inconsistent end‑to‑end user experiences across regions and products.

risks.title: Program‑level cost pressure from potential dual system usage and licensing
risks.description: LatAm Top of Funnel has identified a risk of dual licensing exposure if quoting, renewals, or service remain in S2E while sales moves to GSI, with leadership indicating no appetite for additional licensing costs. Similar patterns (parallel usage of legacy SFDC and new platforms) may occur in Legal Tracker and Special Offers during transition periods, creating a broader program‑level risk around cost and operating model (dual systems).

risks.title: Enterprise data readiness and quality for multi‑project migrations
risks.description: Multiple projects in the Legacy Product Migration program depend on enterprise data being ready and of sufficient quality for migration: LATAM data readiness has not been validated in ~3 years; Legal Tracker relies on EDL to complete migration of all in‑scope data from legacy SFDC; Special Offers – Migration to OC depends on sample and full data availability in EPM and SAP. These dependencies create a program‑level risk that data may not be ready or may be incomplete/inaccurate when needed.

risks.title: Program‑level scheduling and resource conflicts across overlapping 2026 milestones
risks.description: Key milestones for LatAm Top of Funnel, Legal Tracker Migration, and Special Offers – Migration to OC overlap in mid‑ to late‑2026 (build, data migration, SIT/UAT, and go‑lives). Many of these rely on the same enterprise platform teams (GSI, SAP, ECM, EPM, data/EDL). Without coordinated planning, the same specialists may be needed at the same time by multiple projects, creating a program‑level schedule and resource conflict.

entities.name: Pagero Integration
entities.status: Program to deliver end‑to‑end CIO and Product Engineering integration for Pagero in order to meet the new French e‑invoicing/e‑reporting regulatory mandate by 1 September 2026. This includes: (1) building and operating the S3NS environments (test, pre‑prod, prod) required for Pagero; (2) implementing compliant eSSO/MFA capability and securing EU‑based operational support for the new tool; (3) completing legal entity migrations (Belgium, Italy, Poland) and associated SAP releases supporting the mandate; (4) achieving PDP certification, including a mid‑year audit with external French auditors; and (5) completing CIO integration of business systems (lead‑to‑order, coterm, bridge, customer‑to‑cash and partnership management) and transitioning those streams into BAU by the end of May 2026.

risks.title: Linux developer laptops not compliant in Intune may cause audit failures and security exposure
risks.description: A large number of Linux laptops used by Pagero developers dropped out of Intune because users did not log into the Intune app at least monthly. Re‑enrolling these devices into Intune is encountering errors and progressing very slowly, with different issues occurring on each laptop. Approximately 100 Linux laptops are currently not Intune‑managed, and there is poor visibility into the exact number because Intune is not functioning correctly for them. While day‑to‑day end‑user work is not currently impacted, this creates a compliance gap and a risk that non‑managed or even private Linux devices could be used to access customer data.

risks.title: Lack of Wiz support in SANS may delay required cloud security coverage for S3NS
risks.description: The Wiz security solution is currently not supported by SANS in the targeted environment. Bill communicated that there is no firm plan yet for how this will be addressed, despite a policy requirement to have this resolved by 2026. Recent discussions with Google (around 22 April) did not yield a clear delivery timeline for support. If support is significantly delayed, the project may lack the desired level of cloud security visibility and control, and compensating controls may be required.

risks.title: Light LLM deactivation and Zscaler certificate refresh may disrupt Linux developer productivity around June 12 go-live
risks.description: Many Pagero engineers use Linux laptops and rely on Zscaler and the Light LLM integration to work with cloud resources (including Claude). As the June 12 S3NS production go-live approaches, Linux developers have experienced issues migrating to a new Zscaler version, leading some to lose one to two days of productivity and others to roll back to older configurations to avoid further disruption. At the same time, a company-wide Zscaler certificate refresh was scheduled for 4 June, and Light LLM was communicated as being deactivated on 30 May. Although a workaround is available and platform engineering has indicated that Light LLM will remain active until the issue is resolved, there is still a risk that either the cert refresh or eventual Light LLM deactivation will disrupt Linux developer access and tooling during a critical period for S3NS readiness and France go-live preparation.

risks.title: Ceiling Tiles Damage During Cabling or WAP Installation
risks.description: During site surveys for cabling or fixing wireless access points (WAPs), there is a risk of ceiling tiles coming out and being damaged, as evidenced by a recent incident at the Stockholm site.

risks.title: Linux developer laptops not fully managed in Intune may cause audit non-compliance and access restrictions
risks.description: A substantial number of Linux laptops used by Pagero engineering/product teams have dropped out of Intune or are not currently enrolled, and attempts to re-enroll them are encountering varied errors. Approximately 100 Linux devices are estimated to be non-Intune-managed, and the ETS team has treated remediation as low priority. This creates uncertainty about which devices exist within TR and whether private devices are being used, posing compliance risks for multiple audits and potential issues when conditional access is enabled for single sign-on.

risks.title: Office Integration: ISP Connectivity delivery delays
risks.description: Delays due to the Internet Service Provider (ISP) postponing the link delivery date. Further complications can arise from the need for additional internal cabling works and unresolved issues with the landlord, all of which can contribute to the overall slippage in the schedule.

risks.title: CI/CD Tooling Delay Due to S3NS Resource Dependency
risks.description: Pagero resources are presently concentrating on client onboarding to the S3NS environment. At the request of Principal Architect Bard L., activities related to tooling deployment have been temporarily suspended.

risks.title: Public Cloud Strategy Change – 2026
EU-based operations support resources required for Memority eSSO tool
risks.description: ISRM requires three EU-based operations support resources to support the new Memority eSSO/MFA tool used for compliance in the S3NS environment. Recruitment is in progress (one hire starting in July, two candidates in interview), but there is a risk that these resources may not be onboarded and fully productive in time to support pre-prod, prod, and French mandate go-live timelines.

risks.title: Knowledge transfer and onboarding of Memority eSSO ops resources constrained by Swedish vacations
risks.description: New EU-based operations support resources for the Memority eSSO/MFA solution are expected to sign contracts around mid-June 2026, but most Swedish subject matter experts (SMEs) will be out of office through June–July due to holidays. This creates a risk that knowledge transfer, training, and onboarding for these new joiners will be incomplete or delayed, leaving ISRM without sufficient, fully ramped resources to operate Memority ahead of the 1 September 2026 French mandate.

risks.title: Compliant eSSO solution introduction constrained by late-June availability and Swedish vacation period
risks.description: The compliant Memority eSSO solution is expected to be available around the end of June 2026, just before Swedish vacation starts. The infrastructure team advises not introducing this solution right before vacation to avoid requiring Pagero support during a period of limited TR staff availability. There is a risk that the compliant eSSO solution is not live in production by the time customers start processing data, requiring reliance on workarounds and careful control of what data is operated in the environment. As of the 21 May 2026 SteerCo follow-up, the plan is to keep the infrastructure layer on the existing eSSO while starting to use Memority from the application layer, running accounts in parallel to provide fall-back. This implies that S3NS may remain partially non-compliant from an MFA/eSSO perspective through mid-August 2026, extending the previously anticipated non-compliance window and requiring formal risk acceptance from ISRM leadership (including Sofia).

risks.title: Cloud Armor / WAF controls may not be implemented in S3NS production by customer go-live
risks.description: During the 21 May 2026 SteerCo follow-up, Bård highlighted that, in addition to SentinelOne and other ISRM tooling items, ISRM has also raised requirements for cloud application protection via Cloud Armor or an equivalent web application firewall (WAF) in the S3NS environment. Given the current focus on meeting the 12 June 2026 production readiness date and the constraints from Swedish vacations, there is a high likelihood that Cloud Armor/WAF controls will not be deployed in S3NS production by the time customers begin using the environment for live flows, and ISRM will seek a committed implementation date and potentially a formal risk acceptance for the gap period.

risks.title: Security tooling (SentinelOne / Wiz sensor) not fully operational in S3NS environments
risks.description: During S3NS pre-prod setup, SentinelOne was reported as not working properly in the environment. Additionally, Wiz-based agentless scanning remains on the Google/Wiz roadmap and is not yet available, requiring deployment of a local sensor by the Hawk team instead. There is a risk that security tooling will not be fully deployed and functioning by the time S3NS environments need to support production data processing. As of the 21 May 2026 SteerCo follow-up, SentinelOne deployment in S3NS production depends on a Kubernetes cluster upgrade that the Pagero team has scheduled for Q3 2026 to avoid jeopardising the 12 June 2026 production readiness date and to work around Swedish vacation constraints. This means there is a material likelihood that production customer traffic in July–September 2026 will run without full EDR coverage unless compensating controls or an accelerated upgrade are agreed with ISRM. Exposure would be for 3 months - Jul 1 to Sep 30.

At the time of LHR3 closure, the only alternate GlobalScape location available will be MSP, USA. One of the TaxOne customers has a contractual georestriction requirement; must be hosted in EU / UK. This is causing planned work to "concertina" into the second half of 2026. If AWS and TR infrastructure are not available when needed, application migrations (batches 1–3 and pre-work for CAMS) may be delayed, reducing schedule buffer and potentially pushing the overall Sydney colo exit beyond the currently targeted dates (end of 2026 for non‑CAMS apps and mid‑2027 for CAMS and dilapidation).

risks.title: Unproven NAS/FSx integration and user drive-mounting model may cause delays once AMS is available

This pattern, particularly via Zscaler and cloud-based CIFS/SMB shares, has not been fully proven for the Sydney legal content workloads and is considered "not straightforward." If this integration does not work as expected, significant troubleshooting and re-design may be required.

If AD/IAM design and ownership are not resolved early, application access and authentication could become a late-breaking blocker.

actions.title: Abacus/Barossa - Compile and share list of Microsoft Certificate Authorities for Abacus/Barossa to decommission post-migration
