actions.title: Abacus/Barossa - Prepare cost comparison between Azure SQL Managed Instance Gen1 and Gen2 for Abacus/Barossa
actions.description: Develop a cost comparison between Azure SQL Managed Instance Gen1 and Gen2 options for Abacus/Barossa, including the impact of the number of instances, database counts, CPU sizing, and redundancy considerations. Provide this analysis to Pathak, Lalit (TR Technology) so that leadership can review and approve the choice of Gen2 despite the current lack of high availability (HA) within a region.

actions.title: Abacus/Barossa - Create and circulate ADR documenting decision to use Azure SQL Managed Instance Gen2 for Abacus/Barossa
actions.description: Author an Architecture Decision Record (ADR) formally documenting the decision to use Azure SQL Managed Instance Gen2 as the standard for Abacus/Barossa databases, including rationale, constraints (such as lack of intra-region HA until at least 2027), and review/approval by relevant stakeholders. Distribute the ADR for review and confirmation.

actions.title: Abacus/Barossa - Conduct database migration strategy workshop with Ryan, John, and Sridhar
actions.description: Hold the scheduled meeting with Ryan, John, and Duggimpudi, Sridhar (TR Technology) to define the execution strategy for Abacus/Barossa database migrations, including how to handle the split between Abacus and Barossa databases, managed instance sizing, and cutover sequencing.

actions.title: Abacus/Barossa - Confirm Microsoft Certificate Authority involvement not required for Abacus/Barossa Azure/AVD architecture
actions.description: Review the Abacus/Barossa Azure/AVD high-level design and explicitly confirm to Khan, Hammad (TR Technology) that Microsoft Certificate Authority (CA) is not required for this project, providing a clear statement that no Microsoft CA references exist in the architecture diagrams and confirming whether his further involvement is unnecessary. During the 2026-06-08 meeting, Aitchison, Gordon reiterated that Microsoft CA will not be required and agreed that the associated CAs for Abacus and Barossa can be decommissioned after migration, but the action remains open until planning and HLD are formally completed and documented.

actions.title: Abacus/Barossa - Re-baseline Abacus/Barossa migration and LHR3 exit dates after non-prod environments are available and tested
actions.description: Once the non-prod on-prem and Azure/AVD environments are available and the application team under Pathak, Lalit and Duggimpudi, Sridhar has exercised them sufficiently to understand actual migration effort and timelines, develop a revised plan and re-baseline the Abacus/Barossa migration schedule and related LHR3 exit dates. Incorporate any forecast scenarios discussed (including potential slips into 2027) into the updated baseline.

actions.title: General - Provide PMO Partner link and access instructions to Abacus/Barossa stakeholders

actions.title: Abacus/Barossa - Expedite P2B approval for Abacus/Barossa Azure/AVD non-prod environment
actions.description: Monitor and actively follow up on the non-prod P2B approval for the Archon/Azure/AVD environment, engaging approvers as needed to move the request through the process and reduce delays. This now explicitly includes securing Strategy & Governance (S&G) approval for Azure Virtual Desktop (AVD) as a non-strategic product, by ensuring the P2B is submitted before the Wednesday S&G meeting and coordinating with named S&G members.

actions.title: Abacus/Barossa - Obtain Strategy & Governance (S&G) approval for Azure Virtual Desktop usage in Abacus/Barossa architecture
actions.description: Ensure that Strategy & Governance (S&G) approval is obtained for using Azure Virtual Desktop (AVD) in the Abacus/Barossa solution, given that AVD is not yet a fully strategic product. This includes submitting the non-prod P2B ahead of the weekly Wednesday S&G meeting, reaching out to identified S&G members (including Kevin Doyle and Barry Neil) to sponsor and expedite the approval, and tracking the approval to completion.

actions.title: Abacus/Barossa - Engage Software Asset Management and Microsoft licensing contacts to clarify SPLA status beyond Nov-2026

risks.title: Alliant onboarding blocked by Rightsline platform change and lack of integration options like APIs
risks.description: Rightsline vendor does not support SailPoint integration due to the absence of user administration APIs. As an interim measure, a semi-automated solution is being evaluated, involving replication of application data on TR Snowflake MDS or via a feed file as a read-only connector, with provisioning handled through manual work items. The application can be re-onboarded as fully automated once Rightsline develops the required APIs (no ETA shared by vendor).

risks.title: Tool duplication and fragmented adoption across ICFR tooling ecosystem
risks.description: Multiple tools (Protecht, ADO, SharePoint, legacy repositories, DoubleCheck) currently support overlapping ICFR activities without a clear target-state architecture, risking continued duplication and fragmented adoption even after the transformation.

risks.title: Change fatigue among control owners participating in ICFR transformation
risks.description: Control owners are already subject to multiple initiatives and may experience change fatigue as new ICFR processes, controls, tooling, and certifications are introduced.

risks.title: PwC may refuse to use internal ICFR tools for audit interactions
risks.description: The external auditor (PwC) has previously been hesitant to use internal tools, and may continue to resist adopting Protecht or related platforms for evidence requests and status updates.

risks.title: Service Management competing priorities may delay Port Authority work
risks.description: Competing priorities for Service Management work create a risk: Service Management needs prioritization away from the company‑wide migration to Azure and onto Port Authority work. If this does not happen, the Port Authority deadline may not be met.

risks.title: Inadequate or outdated HIPAA policies, BAAs, training, and breach notification processes
risks.description: Policies, contract templates (BAAs/BASAs), training procedures, and breach notification playbooks are being reviewed and updated as part of the HIPAA program. Until updates are complete and rolled out, there is a risk that current materials may not reflect the desired future state or regulatory expectations.

risks.title: Over-scoping of ICFR due to conservative posture
risks.description: The organization may continue to define an overly broad ICFR scope, including excessive controls and application coverage, due to conservative risk and audit postures, despite transformation efforts to rationalize.

risks.title: HighQ: Pen testing may exceed QA testing dates
risks.description: The full Pen testing completion dates will fall outside of the QA testing date window. This could put timelines at risk.

risks.title: Non-integrated access systems and third-party portals may weaken access governance
risks.description: Some systems are not integrated with SailPoint and rely on manual processes or third-party portals, creating potential gaps in provisioning, certification, and deprovisioning controls within the ICFR scope.

risks.title: HighQ Transparent File Encryption (TFE) implementation for HIPAA within FedRAMP boundary
risks.description: TFE for HIPAA must be defined and implemented appropriately while on the FedRAMP boundary. Developments may be required and were not estimated; documentation and mitigating controls need to be evaluated.

risks.title: WL/PL privacy control requirements and impact not yet understood
risks.description: For WL/PL, the team needs to understand what the requirements are for the 24 privacy controls that have now been approved. This could impact timelines but direction is not yet clear and estimates are still needed.

risks.title: Inconsistent evidence quality across ICFR controls
risks.description: Evidence supporting ICFR controls may vary in quality, completeness, and standardization, which can undermine audit readiness and increase rework during testing and external reviews.

risks.title: Program sprawl and excessive stakeholder model may dilute focus and slow decisions
risks.description: The ICFR transformation program may expand its scope or stakeholder base excessively, resulting in complex governance, slow decision-making, and blurred accountability.

risks.title: Ownership gaps for Internal Audit remediation items may delay completion
risks.description: The May 20, 2026 CIO Internal Audit Remediations baseline report identifies ownership gaps for some of the 17 open Internal Audit remediation items. Where accountable owners are ambiguous or not yet assigned, remediation activities may not be actively driven, leading to delays and increased likelihood of items becoming past due and requiring escalation.

risks.title: Resource constraints may prevent timely completion of Internal Audit remediations
risks.description: The baseline report lists resource constraints as a key risk theme for the CIO organization’s open Internal Audit remediation items. Limited availability of staff or competing priorities may prevent remediation work from starting or progressing, particularly for items not yet started and those requiring extensions.

risks.title: Past due remediation items may remain unresolved or lack recovery plans
risks.description: The CIO Internal Audit Remediations report notes that there are past due items; two are close to closure and three require recovery plans. If these items are not promptly closed or given formal recovery plans, they may remain overdue and continue to expose the organization to control and compliance risk.

risks.title: Cloudflare setup on CARI commercial side may be delayed due to Ops team inexperience
risks.description: Cloudflare setup on the CARI commercial side is being performed by the Ops team for the first time. Because the team has not done this work before, there is a learning curve that may impact delivery timelines for the dual-region CARI commercial environment that underpins CoCounsel services.

risks.title: Sungard Avantgard Integrity onboarding blocked by lack of APIs for integration
risks.description: For Sungard Avantgard Integrity, the team is waiting for a delivery date for an enhanced API. FIS vendor is not engaged in a development role, hence currently there is nobody to build the necessary APIs for SialPoint integration.

risks.title: Remediation items due June 30, 2026 may miss their deadlines due to incomplete plans or pending owner responses
risks.description: Several remediation items are coming due by the end of June 2026. The baseline report notes that some of these, including specific items, have not started and have owner responses pending or require extensions. Without confirmed remediation plans and timely owner engagement, these items may not be completed by their June 30, 2026 due dates.

risks.title: Required extensions for remediation items may not be submitted in time
risks.description: The baseline report states that five remediation items require or are likely to require extensions, but no formal extension requests have been submitted as of May 2026. This creates a risk that items will pass their due dates without approved extensions, breaching audit commitments.

risks.title: Competing priorities may limit product and operational teams’ capacity for HIPAA assessment and remediation
risks.description: Product and operational teams may have limited bandwidth due to competing priorities, which could constrain their ability to participate in HIPAA assessments, scope validation, and remediation work.

risks.title: Variability in product architectures and data flows may prevent a single uniform HIPAA solution
risks.description: Products and services differ in architectures, data flows, and contractual commitments, which may make it difficult to implement a single standardized HIPAA compliance solution across all in-scope areas.

risks.title: Phased implementation may extend beyond initial project window
risks.description: The need for phased implementation across multiple products and services means that full HIPAA compliance maturity may require stages beyond the initial project timeline (2025-07-07 to 2027-12-31).

risks.title: CIAM orchestration token correctness may delay CARI integration and customer onboarding
risks.description: Previously, CIAM integration and customer onboarding for Port Authority products were blocked not by architecture but by token correctness. An authentication gap in CIAM orchestration tokens required for CARI integration prevented completion of integration with the new legacy token service.

risks.title: Unclear decisions on signing BAAs/BASAs during discovery and remediation phases
risks.description: The program has not yet finalized decisions on whether to sign BAAs/BASAs for in-scope products during the discovery phase or before remediation is complete, and whether to unwind existing contracts for products without valid PHI use cases.

risks.title: IAM/CoCounsel tight coupling with HighQ limits failover and failback options
risks.description: If IAM/CoCounsel remains tightly coupled with HighQ under the chosen hosting model, single‑component failover/failback will be limited, which is acknowledged as a constraint of the chosen hosting model.

risks.title: FIPS cryptography requirements may cause microservice startup issues
risks.description: FIPS cryptography requirements may cause application startup issues, requiring additional joint troubleshooting; this is a current technical challenge for the microservices.

risks.title: HighQ and Contract Express resourcing at risk due to incomplete effort estimation
risks.description: There is a risk to approved HighQ and Contract Express resourcing because estimation of the effort to meet the Port Authority contract is not complete.

risks.title: HighQ and Contract Express deliverables at risk due to unresolved effort estimation and add-in scope
risks.description: There is a risk to previously committed HighQ and Contract Express deliverables because estimation of the effort to meet the Port Authority contract is not complete, and the work required for the CoCounsel for MS Outlook Add‑in is not yet understood.

risks.title: HighQ antivirus tool Sophos may not meet FedRAMP FIPS 140‑2/3 requirements
risks.description: Sophos, an antivirus/security tool currently used by HighQ, has not been confirmed as compliant with FedRAMP requirements, specifically around FIPS 140‑2/3 encryption compliance. A similar issue previously required another internal team to abandon ClamAV and switch tools. If Sophos cannot prove compliance, HighQ may need to replace it with a different tool such as SentinelOne or Azure Defender, which could impact the engineering timeline.

risks.title: Project is not prioritized for the Service Management team.
risks.description: Competing priorities keep the work of permanent user role creation from starting.

risks.title: HighQ antivirus scanning tool selection (Sophos / SentinelOne / Defender) remains unresolved
risks.description: For HighQ (and related CoCounsel integrations), identifying and validating a compliant antivirus/malware scanning tool is still in progress. Options under evaluation include Sophos, SentinelOne, and Microsoft Defender. License procurement has been completed, but verification of the selected solution against FedRAMP FIPS 140‑2/3 and Port Authority requirements is ongoing, including a planned FARB discussion on the Sophos solution.

risks.title: Cloudflare setup on the CARI commercial side may be delayed due to Ops team inexperience
risks.description: Cloudflare setup on the CARI commercial side is being performed by the Ops team for the first time. Because the team has not done this work before, there is a learning curve that may impact delivery timelines for the dual‑region CARI commercial environment that underpins CoCounsel services.

risks.title: RAS Dual Region team bandwidth constraints may delay dual-region delivery
risks.description: The RAS Dual Region workstream is constrained by insufficient team bandwidth due to org-level resource changes. Team members were moved to other projects (e.g., Catalyst and AIESE), and remaining staff are spread thin across multiple initiatives.

risks.title: FedRAMP vulnerability remediation may not achieve significant progress by end of June 2026
risks.description: Legal Research/Risk & Fraud (WL/PL) and CoCounsel FedRAMP environments still have thousands of outstanding vulnerabilities across FedRAMP and RAS-FedRAMP Plexus Service Mesh. Although overall trends are improving, recent sprints showed increases in remaining vulnerabilities, and teams note that achieving consistent sprint-cadence container refreshes and vulnerability reduction will be a struggle until a stable process is in place. There is a risk that the program will not achieve the targeted 'significant progress' in vulnerability reduction by the end of June 2026 needed for HHS FedRAMP ATO.

risks.title: Lack of clarity from FedRamp-based HIPAA assessments for C-Track and Case Center
risks.description: For C-Track and Case Center, Fortreum conducted assessments within the FedRamp space, but the reports did not provide clear remediation guidance for identified HIPAA gaps.

risks.title: Potential gaps in SIU Professional Services remediation execution
risks.description: Although the SIU Professional Services HIPAA assessment is complete and a remediation plan has been developed, remediation is staged through the end of 2026, and not all gaps will be resolved by mid-2026.

risks.title: Legal Tracker remediation year-end deadlines
risks.description: The Legal Tracker HIPAA assessment is complete, and remediation planning is underway with deadlines expected by year-end.

risks.title: HighQ: CSPP – Microsoft program requirement for WOPI (8 week expected time) – request submitted
risks.description:
For continuity of service within the new HighQ Azure Gov environment of our Open-in-Office-for-the-Web/WOPI integration, we are required to submit a CSPP environment change request to Microsoft. 
 
This request has been submitted and normally this process should take 4-5 weeks for Microsoft to complete, however, they informed us May 22 that, due to issues on their side with Office deployment via CSPP, this could now take up to 8 weeks. 
 
Despite detailed conversations with Microsoft over the last 3 months in relation to this service, we weren't previously informed of this requirement, however, we are doing all we can to expedite execution via Microsoft as quickly as possible.  
 
As a result, it is likely the Open-in-Office-for-the-Web capability will not be available immediately upon release of the HighQ instance to PANYNJ and work-arounds may need to be employed (e.g. download documents, then edit locally) in the interim period.

risks.title: June 30 Port Authority compliance timeline may not be met for HighQ and Contract Express

risks.title: Partial approval of full 2027 EPC funding request for all products

risks.description: Key finance, operations, business, compliance, IT, and audit stakeholders may not have sufficient time to participate in workshops, reviews, and approvals, which could slow or stall the design, validation, and implementation of the modernized ICFR operating model.

entities.name: CIAM Migrations
entities.status: CIAM Migrations is a multi‑year program to modernize and consolidate customer identity and access management across Thomson Reuters by moving all legacy IDP and SSO solutions to the CIAM platform. The program coordinates federated SSO migrations, local user migrations (such as ONESOURCE, OnePass and other products like SafeSend, etc), and enabling CIAM features to deliver a unified, secure, and simplified sign-in experience across products.
entities.okrs: Migrate 65% of all SSO customers by Dec 31, 2026 (all legacy IDPs). Migrate 100% of OnePass accounts (SSO and Local) to CIAM by Dec 31, 2026.

risks.title: Customer resistance to proposed SSO migration timelines
risks.description: Some customers may not be willing to migrate their SSO connections on the timeline proposed in the 2026–2027 TR Account / CIAM migration roadmap.

risks.title: 65% 2026 CIAM migration target (including OnePass) may not be achievable with current customer engagement and outreach capacity
risks.description: There is a significant risk that the program will not achieve the 2026 objective of migrating 65% of legacy SSO connections to CIAM and completing the OnePass SSO migration. Current customer response rates remain extremely low (reported as below 0.5% progress in executive reporting), the outreach vetting process is slow due to difficulty identifying the correct CSM/Account Specialist for each account, and communications volume, while increasing, is still only in the hundreds of emails per month. Leadership is questioning whether the 65% + full OnePass target is realistic even under the optimistic assumption that 100% of customers agree to migrate, given constraints on team capacity, customer engagement, and sequencing across products (OnePass, SafeSend, OneSource, Legal Tracker, etc.).

risks.title: Hybrid TR Account / legacy SSO states from partial federation may create long-term security and technical debt issues
risks.description: To accelerate meeting migration targets, the team is considering a "partial federation" / multi-connection approach where customers are migrated off OnePass for specific legal or OneSource products, while other Thomson Reuters Account (TRA/CIAM) products for the same customer remain on local (non-federated) credentials. In this model, a single customer can be left in a hybrid state for an extended period (some users/products federated, others not). During the May 29, 2026 weekly status meeting, Peter Grigoriou and Jeff Olson noted that many customers may be comfortable remaining in this hybrid state, while Harvarinder Batth expressed concern that once such configurations are in place they may persist "for the next 10 or 20 years," effectively becoming long-lived technical debt and potentially creating security gaps if customers assume all access is federated and centrally controlled.

risks.title: Delay in SAP product team implementing CIAM-only onboarding for new accounts may expand OnePass footprint and create rework
risks.description: For Co Counsel customers interested in Anthropic MCP and related AI features, the long-term plan is that all new accounts will be created as CIAM-only by default, regardless of sales channel. Sales leaders (Kristine and Marie) agree with this direction, but the SAP product team (owned by Kyle in the Amy Hutsell group) has not yet committed to delivering the required feature to stop creating new OnePass accounts. In the interim (next ~1.5 months), new accounts continue to be created on OnePass, requiring manual migration before MCP can be enabled and adding operational overhead and noise. Although the OnePass team is planning to deliver an API in mid-June that SAP can leverage, SAP’s implementation timing remains uncertain.

risks.title: Identity divergence and data master misalignment during CIAM migration for non-migrated ONESOURCE platform tenants
risks.description: When new users are created in ONESOURCE (OSP) tenants that have not yet been enabled for CIAM migration, the system automatically creates a parallel CIAM identity as part of a standardized backend flow. These two identities — OSP and CIAM — are independent with no enforced synchronization. If a user's email is subsequently changed in OSP but not in CIAM (or vice versa), the systems treat the updated email as a new, separate identity. This creates a compounding risk of duplicate identities, broken access, and data master misalignment — particularly once tenants are migrated and CIAM becomes the system of record.

risks.title: ONESOURCE products who leverage OData connections are unable to have users who license the product migrate
risks.description: There is no solution to migrate OData connectors to CIAM yet, putting the migration of customers using them at risk.

risks.title: Scaling migration execution and coordination across customer-facing teams
risks.description: As the program enters large-scale migration (non-SSO and non-basic auth tenants), scaling execution across the customer base may be constrained by the need for stronger coordination among account managers, support teams, marketing, and other customer-facing organizations.

risks.title: Limited reliability of legacy IDP user metrics may undermine CIAM migration planning and tracking
risks.description: Some legacy IDPs, such as certain platforms referenced in the CIAM reporting appendix (e.g., Checkpoint and others), have historically provided limited or unreliable data on key metrics, including the number of users being migrated and the number of users per federated customer IDP. Obtaining this data, even upon request, can be challenging, and tracking it on an ongoing basis is likely to be complex and resource-intensive.

risks.title: Customer readiness for API user migration timelines
risks.description: API user migration work is funded and in development with the API Guild team (development targeted for Q4 2026 and migrations starting Q1 2027), but there is a concern that customers may not be ready to adopt the new API authentication timelines.

risks.title: Ping Federate performance and UI limitations may delay SSO configuration and CIAM migrations
risks.description: Ping Federate is exhibiting performance and UI issues when handling large numbers of configured URLs and connections. Pages listing thousands of customer URLs are taking a very long time to load and intermittently timing out, which in turn causes errors and delays when the customer SSO team attempts to configure new CIAM SSO connections or modify existing ones. These issues are affecting not only CIAM migration work but any customer SSO configuration activity that relies on Ping, and are causing setup cycles to take significantly longer than expected. Although a workaround exists and some remediation work is planned (including a change being deployed the night of June 5, 2026), there is a risk that these problems persist or recur, creating ongoing friction and delay in enabling SSO for CIAM migrations.

risks.title: Anthropic MCP migration intake handled by single SME may create capacity bottleneck and weekend coverage gaps
risks.description: Anthropic MCP-related migration requests for Co Counsel Legal/Next are currently funneled through a single intake process that is being manually reviewed and actioned primarily by Harvarinder Batth. Requests arrive via a new form and require checking whether accounts are SSO or local, obtaining customer approval to migrate to CIAM, and then handing off to Kim for inclusion in nightly migration waves. There is no weekend/holiday coverage in place yet, and Harv is considering checking requests hourly or every two hours. Leadership explicitly called out that Harv is a potential single point of failure and that early in the process there could be 72-hour windows (e.g., long weekends) where customers receive no response. This could undermine the opportunity to capitalize on strong inbound demand from Anthropic MCP users who are "fish wanting to jump into the boat."

risks.title: HighQ product team deprioritization may leave ~700 legacy HighQ SSO connections unmigrated within CIAM program timelines
risks.description: During the June 5, 2026 status meeting, Harvarinder Batth and Eduardo Cuevas reported that the HighQ product team does not currently prioritize migrating their legacy SSO customers to CIAM. HighQ is not on OnePass and has approximately 600–700 legacy SSO connections that would need to be moved to TR Account (CIAM). The HighQ team is in the middle of two other migrations, faces resource constraints, and has recently encountered issues when migrating customers to CIAM/SSO, leading them to pause proactive outreach. They indicated that they intend to perform further analysis and only plan to restart planning at the end of Q3 2026, with no firm migration deadline or schedule. There is a risk that HighQ migrations slip beyond the life of the central SSO migration team or are indefinitely delayed, leaving a large block of connections on legacy SSO and undermining CIAM migration objectives.

risks.title: Client Communication Approach May Negatively Impact SSO Migration Adoption and Timeline
risks.description: Client-facing communications for the SSO migration program are currently perceived as overly aggressive, unclear, and not aligned with premium client engagement standards. Feedback indicates issues with tone, short response timelines, time zone mismatches, and lack of coordination with local account teams. This may lead to confusion, reduced trust, and delayed client responses.

risks.title: Residual unmigrated local user profiles may undermine completion of CIAM local user migrations
risks.description: Although 98% of local user accounts are in forced migration, many individual profiles within those accounts remain unmigrated due to user behavior and profile quality factors (inactive, invalid, or very infrequent users). This may prevent the program from achieving full local user migration coverage.

risks.title: ONESOURCE: Not having dedicated bandwidth from CSM/Account managers, Support and Marketing does not allow the migration process to scale across a large number of tenants on ONESOURCE
risks.description: Not having dedicated bandwidth from CSM/Account managers, Support and Marketing does not allow the migration process to scale across a large number of tenants on ONESOURCE to assist with the migration to CIAM.

risks.title: ONESOURCE Migration: Basic Auth Remediation of some ONESOURCE products blocking CIAM migration
risks.description:
Some of the product teams with basic auth scenarios are either blocked or have remediation timelines going well into Q2 2026. Other products are experiencing delays with the required remediation. This blocks the migration effort given that the customers who subscribe to these products will not be able to move to CIAM. This impacts 45% tenants in AMER, 80% in EMEA and 90% in APAC.
Products that need to be remediated: OCT legacy, OCT NG (EMEA), OIA CoCounsel, OIT Data Import AddIn, OIT Automation test suite, OSR, OSR Desktop, TAXONE

risks.description: Following outreach, only about 25% of customers are engaging and agreeing to migration timelines. Since federated (SSO) user migrations depend on customers accepting proposed schedules, sustained low agreement rates may prevent the CIAM Migrations program from achieving its planned migration volumes and overall timeline.

risks.title: SSO Migration: OnePass End of Life Statement agreement and sign off from stakeholders
risks.description: In order to publish the OnePass End of Life Statement, various leaders and stakeholders need to sign off on the statement. If we do not gain agreement, we will not be able to publish the End of Life Statement that will encourage customers to migrate

risks.description: Some of the product teams with basic auth scenarios (current calls to generate UDSLongToken via username/password (i.e., the /fromusermodel endpoint) are either blocked or have remediation timelines going well into Q2 2026. Other products are experiencing delays with the required remediation. This blocks the migration effort given that the customers who subscribe to these products will not be able to move to CIAM. This impacts 45% tenants in AMER, 80% in EMEA and 90% in APAC.

risks.title: Product-by-product (partial) SSO migrations may create long-term hybrid security and technical debt for CIAM
risks.description: During the May 29, 2026 OnePass–CIAM Migration Weekly Status Meeting, the team discussed accelerating SSO migration progress by enabling customers to migrate on a product-by-product basis (e.g., moving Legal Tracker or ONESOURCE SSO connections off OnePass to CIAM) while leaving other TR Account products for the same customer on local credentials or non-federated states. This "multi-connection" approach would allow counting those product connections as migrated for CIAM OKR purposes, even if the customer remains in a hybrid state where some users are federated and others are not. While this could improve near-term migration metrics, leadership (Harvarinder, Peter, Jeff) expressed concern that customers may assume deprovisioning and access controls are fully centralized when they are not, and that hybrid configurations may remain indefinitely due to funding and prioritization constraints, creating long-lived security and technical debt across products.

risks.description: Customer migrations often involve more complicated account-level licensing and configuration scenarios than originally planned. This complexity spans multiple products and platforms that are part of the CIAM Migrations program and can slow both SSO and local user migrations.

issues.title: Program-level issue: Low customer engagement and agreement on CIAM migration timelines

issues.title: Program-level issue: Limited and unreliable user metrics from some legacy IDPs complicate CIAM progress tracking

Obtaining this information, even upon request, may present challenges, and tracking it on an ongoing basis is likely to be complex and resource-intensive.

issues.title: Ping Federate UI performance issues delaying SSO connection setup
issues.description: Ping Federate is experiencing UI performance and timeout issues when loading pages with large numbers of configured URLs for customers, causing delays and intermittent errors during SSO connection setup. Administrators sometimes receive errors and must retry actions, slowing down configuration of CIAM/SSO connections for new and migrating customers.

issues.title: Unmigrated profiles within forced migration local user accounts

issues.title: Low customer response rate continues to impact CIAM migration progress
issues.description: Customer response to CIAM migration outreach remains below the level required to support the planned migration from legacy IDPs to TR Account (CIAM), though some improvements are being observed as outreach is accelerated and templates are strengthened.

issues.title: Difficulty Identifying Account Specialist / CSM Ownership for Customer Accounts
issues.description:
The project team is facing significant challenges identifying the appropriate Account Specialist (ASM) or Customer Success Manager (CSM) for each customer account requiring SSO migration follow-up and escalation.

The required account ownership information is spread across multiple systems and is not aggregated or centralized. Many of these systems support only specific customer segments, such as Corporates, Legal, and Tax, or sometimes only a single product area, such as Legal Tracker. As a result, the team is unable to easily determine the correct ASM or CSM contact for each account.

This has created a highly manual and time-consuming process, requiring the team to review accounts one by one and coordinate with multiple teams and data analysis resources to locate the correct account owner.

Delivering this milestone allows the ONESOURCE team to end usage of a legacy MFA system that is no longer being used by any other team at Thomson Reuters.
ONESOURCE migrations to CIAM for all regular users (not MFA, not SSO, not OData, no basic auth scenarios)

Wording in customer comms have been strengthened and more customers are being reached out to than originally planned. risks.title: Complexity and architectural blockers in transferring Noetica AWS accounts into TR AWS organization
risks.description: Transferring Noetica AWS accounts into the Thomson Reuters (TR) AWS organization requires decomposing AWS Control Tower and Identity Center usage at the Noetica org root, recreating OUs, and changing the account provisioning model. The Noetica team highlighted multiple technical concerns: heavy dependency on Control Tower and Identity Center, IAM role and org ID dependencies, CloudFront/WAF behavior, GPU capacity reservations, logging aggregation, and the lack of an easy rollback path if issues occur. Identity Center was called out as a major blocker because it must run at the org root, which conflicts with TR’s current FedRAMP constraints. If these complexities are underestimated or not fully mitigated, the org transfer project may cause subtle production breakages or stall indefinitely.

The extraction query does not pick up on "deployment-engine" and "simple_static_content_deployer" service types. (owners: Cumulus Dev + PORT Team)

risks.title: Loopio tool GenAI expectations misaligned and AI feature enablement delayed
risks.description: There is a risk that expectations for Loopio’s GenAI capabilities are misaligned and AI feature enablement is delayed due to contract negotiations and configuration uncertainty. Until AI functionality is activated, the CT team must perform more manual work.

risks.title: Unresolved ServiceNow CI–service association behaviour may block cutover from Datadog incidents
risks.description: During the May 12, 2026 AIOps Product Onboarding regional sync, the team observed that ServiceNow is not associating services with the correct CIs for large applications such as Legal Tracker. Internal analysis suggests that a configurable limit of approximately 1,000 CIs per service causes additional CIs to be handled via dynamic CI groups, which in turn prevents correct service association and grouping. ServiceNow’s consultant (Doug) indicated there are “traverse rules” that might address this but needs to consult CMDB experts. Until a clear recommendation and fix are in place, the Legal Tracker product team considers this a showstopper for disabling Datadog-direct incident creation.

risks.title: Incorrect priority and severity mapping from Datadog to ServiceNow incidents
risks.description: Priority and severity values from Datadog monitors are not yet consistently or correctly mapped into ServiceNow alert and incident fields. Severity has sometimes been populated from unexpected payload fields, custom test fields exist, and the mapping between Datadog alert_priority/alert_type and ServiceNow severity, impact, urgency, and priority is still being designed. If this is not resolved before enabling automated incident creation, incidents may be mis‑prioritized.

risks.title: Lack of monitoring governance and standardized thresholds across products
risks.description: There is no centralized event management practice or monitoring governance. Platform Engineering publishes Datadog policies on SharePoint but does not audit or enforce them. Thresholds and configurations vary by product; 80% of monitors are synthetics with product‑specific thresholds, and 75% of GCC events come from one product (HighQ). Many teams do not understand event threshold concepts (informational/warning/critical).

risks.title: Project sponsor absence and team restructuring may delay near-term deliverables
risks.description: There is a risk that the project sponsor’s three‑month absence (Late March- late June) and associated restructuring of the project team and decision-making model will extend timelines for near-term deliverables due to limited strategy and domain context among new team members. Mitigation date: TBD as this is an on ongoing planning and knowledge transfer effort.

risks.title: Departure of key AIOps architect (Chris Rutherford) may impact continuity and governance
risks.description: During the 30-Apr-2026 regular sync, Jot and the team thanked Chris Rutherford and noted that he would not be on the project from the following day. Chris has been the primary architect and leadership liaison for the ServiceNow AIOps/Event Management design, including incident priority behaviour, governance model, onboarding approach, and alignment with the Datadog hygiene programme. His departure creates a risk that architectural context, design rationale, and decision history may be lost or diluted, slowing future rule changes, onboarding of new products, and governance maturation.

risks.title: High concentration of noise from HighQ overshadowing other Tier 1 services
risks.description: 75% of GCC monthly events come from a single product (HighQ) out of ~50 Tier 1 products. If this concentration of noise is not addressed, it will continue to dominate GCC workload and may mask important events from other services, even after Event Management is enabled.

risks.title: Datadog and ServiceNow event volume and storage constraints
risks.description: There are concerns about the volume of events if all Datadog accounts send events into ServiceNow. While Datadog does not charge egress fees, ServiceNow storage is finite (e.g., ~4TB per instance), and high event volume could consume storage and impact performance if retention and filtering strategies are not defined.

risks.title: Agent chat PROD Functionality Failing
risks.description: Core Agent Chat functionality failing in PROD Check Ticket & Support Status” works in DEV/QA but not in PROD

risks.title: Teams without Event Management access losing visibility during cutover
risks.description: Not all operational teams (e.g., Major Incident team) currently have access to the Event Management module and dashboards. If the legacy Datadog–driven incident creation is disabled before those teams have alternative visibility, they may not see or manage critical events during and after cutover.

risks.title: CI binding from events/alerts to CMDB CIs may not work reliably
risks.description: Despite existing CIs in the CMDB with matching names, ServiceNow’s out‑of‑the‑box CI identification and binding logic is often failing to associate incoming Datadog events/alerts with the correct CI records.

risks.title: Legal Tracker monitor priorities and severities may not align with TR standards needed for AIOps
risks.description: Legal Tracker’s Datadog monitors currently have impact, urgency, and priority configured in Terraform, but those settings may not align with the TR incident priority matrix or with what AIOps expects to calculate severity/priority in ServiceNow.

risks.title: Agent chat interaction visibility model may not support desired multi-agent access
risks.description: Jakub requested investigating whether the same interaction conversation can be available to multiple agents at once, which is not the default behavior of Advanced Work Assignment (AWA). Current understanding is that supervisors/managers can join ongoing interactions, but it is unclear whether the system can be configured so different agents can pick up the same interaction, or if timing parameters (e.g., 1-minute search interval) must be adjusted instead.

risks.title: SAP Coding Assistant - Productivity/Benefits realization
Correct Road Map
risks.description: ServiceDesk case does not have a firm roadmap in place on how VC outcomes will be achieved in 2027 regarding HCL Insource/Renegotiation. Commit to 2026/2027 service desk delivery roadmap, backwards-planned from December 2027 and from the HCL-renegotiation date

risks.title: Benefit Mechanism
risks.description: Comm Eng benefits assumptions are tied to a contract model change (T&M → SOW + AI clauses) - outside the program’s direct control and may face attribution challenges

risks.title: Production go-live before Event Management configuration and plugins are stable
risks.description: Event rules, respond rules, CI binding logic, and some plugins/scheduled jobs in upper environments are still under active revision. Doug has had to rebuild event rules from scratch due to conflicting behaviors, and some plugins in cloned environments require repair. There is pressure to meet the April 1, 2026 go‑live date for AIOps Event Management.

risks.title: Event forwarding between ServiceNow production and lower environments will function for test data
risks.description: The team is planning to use ServiceNow’s event forwarding from the production instance to dev and QA so that lower environments receive representative Datadog event traffic for testing rules and correlation without needing separate Datadog integrations for each environment.

risks.title: Agent chat access/role configuration for HCL testers not fully working
risks.description: Some HCL users (e.g., Kandibanda Rakesh, Sri Lakshmi and others) cannot see or use the agent chat widget despite being added to the "Nava pilot users" / HCL groups with required roles. Causes appear related to legacy membership in HCL service desk groups and/or roles not propagating correctly from groups to users. If unresolved, HCL agents will not be able to perform hands-on testing of agent chat end-to-end.

risks.title: Agent capacity and presence configuration may overload or mis-route chats
risks.description: Advanced Work Assignment (AWA) agent presence and capacity settings are not yet properly configured. Many agents appear as "available" indefinitely (even after being inactive for long periods), and default capacities (e.g., number of parallel chats per agent) are effectively unset or inconsistent. This can cause the system to treat long-inactive agents as available capacity and over-assign chats beyond reasonable limits.

risks.title: Delayed monitor and tag standardization for GTM4 and SIAM may slip AIOps onboarding timelines
risks.description: GTM4 and SIAM subject-matter experts have expressed concerns that they may not be able to complete required Datadog monitor/tag standardization work (FinOpsDatadogAlerts updates, Asset Insight ID, primary support group, TR API name tags) by the targeted dates (end of this week / May 18). Luis has begun making some standardization changes, but key inputs such as synthetic monitor design and TR API name still depend on product teams. Without those updates, the AIOps webhook cannot be enabled because payloads would lack required fields, preventing correct grouping, routing, and service identification for these products.

risks.title: Missing Service Associations in AIOps-generated incidents may delay Datadog cutover
risks.description: Legal Tracker incidents created via AIOps in ServiceNow are missing service associations (impacted service mappings) or have them populated incorrectly. As of 12-May, this is called out as an LT blocker and work-in-progress item owned by Doug, with the project explicitly stating that Datadog direct incident creation cannot be cut off until the service association issue is resolved.

risks.title: FedRAMP governance and plugin enablement may constrain or delay AIOps usage in regulated environments
risks.description: For FedRAMP, the team must complete governance and compliance documentation (a spreadsheet demonstrating controls and processes) and has opted in to all relevant ServiceNow plugins ahead of a platform clone over the weekend. Tim expects no significant change impact, but until the documentation is accepted and post-clone behaviour is validated, there is residual uncertainty about whether FedRAMP requirements or plugin changes could constrain or delay use of AIOps integrations in regulated environments.

risks.title: Low attendance at wider project team meetings impedes progress
risks.description: Action A22 notes that attendance at wider project team meetings has been poorly represented, leading to a shift toward smaller group sessions per segment to drive forward progress on critical deliverables and timelines.

risks.title: Unvalidated overall project status pending backlog review
risks.description: April 14 meeting notes indicate that the team agreed to reassess overall project status (e.g., On Track/Green) after the backlog review and progress validation. Until this reassessment occurs, the current status may not reflect actual risk and progress.

risks.title: Salesforce Coding Assistant - low adoption (CE AI Coding Agents Efficiency)
risks.description: Usage reports indicate low adoption of the Salesforce Coding Assistant despite rollout and completion of training. Recent discussions highlight that Agentforce (Salesforce AI assistant) is moving to a licensed model with unclear licensing and/or alternative tool strategy, which may further depress adoption and complicate measurement.

risks.title: Lack of standardized Datadog monitor configuration and observability governance may hinder AIOps rollout
risks.description: Datadog monitors across Thomson Reuters are owned by many different teams without a single centralized observability practice. Priority, severity, tags, and other configuration standards are inconsistently applied, and many monitors are configured primarily for escalation convenience (e.g., over‑using P1/P2).

risks.title: Infeasibility of effective governance with 110+ Datadog organizations
risks.description: The team questioned whether effective governance is feasible with over 110 Datadog organizations. The group agreed that governance is significantly harder at this scale and that deeper analysis and architectural discussion are required to determine a sustainable governance model.

risks.title: Insufficient Datadog monitor metadata blocks scalable cleanup
risks.description: Tax, Corporate, and Legal teams have indicated that current Datadog inventory exports do not include critical metadata such as "who created the monitor", "who the monitor is assigned to", and "when the monitor last fired". Dominique reported that Tax explicitly called this a "showstopper" for performing ongoing cleanup of monitors without Asset IDs. Without this metadata, teams cannot efficiently group, prioritize, or assign remediation work across hundreds or thousands of monitors.

risks.title: Single-occurrence Datadog alerts remaining as orphan alerts without incidents
risks.description: ServiceNow AIOps is currently configured so that incidents are only created after grouping multiple alerts. During the 11 May 2026 sync, Luis noted that some alerts are left as 'orphans' because they only occur once and therefore never become part of a multi-alert group that triggers incident creation. Until expectations are clarified with the Legal Tracker team and configuration is adjusted, there is a risk that valid single-occurrence alerts will not generate incidents, reducing visibility into certain issues.

risks.title: Out-of-the-box event and alert rules may not cover all Legal Tracker scenarios
risks.description: The team intends to start with mostly out‑of‑the‑box ServiceNow event rules and a very small number of TR‑specific rules (around three). Some known scenarios, such as monitors triggering on multiple hosts, are not fully addressed yet and cause sub‑optimal grouping.

risks.title: No clear ownership and governance model for Event Management could recreate Datadog ‘mess’
risks.description: There is currently no formally established owner for ServiceNow Event Management and AIOps governance; without this, different teams may create and modify rules, payloads, and processes inconsistently, similar to the fragmented situation in Datadog today.

risks.title: Poor KB/runbook quality limiting AI-driven remediation and playbooks
risks.description: Existing knowledge base articles and runbooks are fragmented, often stored in Azure DevOps wikis, and of uneven quality. The project intends to use ServiceNow AIOps (LEAP, Now Assist) and playbooks for automated or assisted remediation, which depend heavily on reliable KB content and standardized runbooks.

risks.title: Datadog → ServiceNow production connectivity may not be working at go‑live
risks.description: OAuth / webhook connectivity from Datadog production to the ServiceNow production event table may fail (401 errors or authorization issues), preventing events from being ingested when the webhook endpoint is cut over to production.

risks.title: Insufficient Legal Tracker event volume for tuning event rules and correlation
risks.description: Current Legal Tracker monitors are only sending a small number of events (e.g., 40–50) into the ServiceNow dev event table, far below the true number of monitors (~900+). This provides too little variety and volume to reliably design and test event rules, alert grouping, and CI binding before go‑live.

risks.title: Machine-learning-based alert grouping may incorrectly group unrelated alerts and erode trust in AIOps
risks.description: ServiceNow’s machine-learning-based alert grouping is currently grouping unrelated alerts (e.g., a synthetic and an infrastructure monitor) into a single group for Legal Tracker, apparently based on CI relationships. Andrea and Luis observed at least one recent example where the impacted services differed but the alerts were still grouped, and Luis confirmed this grouping did not come from the TR-defined rules but from ServiceNow’s ML logic. If ML continues to group unrelated alerts, Legal Tracker and GCC will not be able to rely on alert groups to understand issues, and teams may push to disable AI features entirely, undermining the value of AIOps.

risks.title: Loss of AIOps program lead may impact configuration and governance continuity
risks.description: Chris Rutherford, the ServiceNow / Platform Engineering leader and de facto program lead for the SNOW AIOps implementation, is leaving the project as of the end of April 2026. Chris has been a key architect for event management design, incident priority behaviour, and governance decisions.
