risks.title: Legal Tracker AIOps implementation fails to deliver incident reduction and customer value
risks.description: Despite Legal Tracker being the pilot product, AIOps/Event Management is not yet delivering the expected reduction in incidents or operational value. As of the April 21, 2026 lessons-learned session, Legal Tracker remains on a 1:1 Datadog alert-to-incident model in production, grouping rules have recently been configured in a way that adds little value (e.g., grouping by Asset Insight ID only), critical data prerequisites (Datadog tags, assignment groups, CMDB CI state) are still being remediated, and clear success criteria and ownership for rule maintenance are only now being defined. If this continues, the Legal Tracker team may not adopt Event Management as a new way of working, and the pilot will not demonstrate the promised benefits for broader rollout.

risks.title: Significant Asset ID coverage gaps in Datadog monitors
risks.description: Based on a February snapshot, about 25% of Datadog monitors lack an associated Asset ID. The team highlighted this as a critical data quality gap and a priority risk, and noted the need for a repeatable approach and ongoing inventory refresh to improve Asset ID coverage.

risks.title: Machine learning-based 'group text' alert grouping may incorrectly combine or misclassify alerts
risks.description: ServiceNow AIOps is applying machine learning ('group text' type) to group alerts based on similarities in alert descriptions. For Legal Tracker, many alert descriptions share similar text patterns, which has led to at least one case where unrelated alerts were grouped together unexpectedly. Because the ML model is tuned on existing data and technical teams are only now learning how to adjust its behaviour, there is a risk that machine learning-based groupings will over-group or mis-group alerts before the configuration and operating model are fully established.

risks.title: Duplicate or inflated incident volumes during AIOps and Datadog parallel run
risks.description: When AIOps/Event Management starts creating incidents from alerts while the existing direct Datadog→ServiceNow incident integration is still active, the same underlying issues may result in multiple incidents or an increased incident count during the transition period.

risks.title: Delayed and non-compliant enablement of AIOps/Event Management in FedRAMP environment
risks.description: During the 11 May 2026 sync, AD asked about enabling AIOps/Event Management in the FedRAMP environment for high-noise FedRAMP applications (including HighQ). Tim Roe confirmed that no AIOps/Event Management work has yet started in FedRAMP and that an assessment is required to mirror enterprise configuration while complying with FedRAMP processes, approvals, and licensing constraints. There is also a need to ensure AI-related configurations (such as do not share data for AI training) are correctly set, as in the enterprise instance.

risks.title: ServiceNow event forwarding limits may cause loss of forwarded events for Datadog-based testing
risks.description: ServiceNow event forwarding from production to lower environments (dev/QA) is configured with both a daily limit and a one-hour time window. HiCase feedback from ServiceNow Support indicates that forwarding does not backfill historical events and respects these limits. During the 30-Apr-2026 regular sync, Yash highlighted that this combination introduces a risk that some Datadog events will not be forwarded (for example, older events outside the one-hour duration or when daily forwarding thresholds are reached), which could lead to missing test data in dev/QA or incomplete visibility if forwarding is used operationally.

risks.title: Program timelines and Phase 1 schedule not yet defined
risks.description: The team acknowledged that target timelines for Phase 1 deliverables and overall Datadog Hygiene program reporting are not yet defined. Timelines are required for reporting, and work needs to be time‑boxed via a backlog, but specific dates have not been set.

risks.title: Automated rollback for Materia
risks.description: Materia has a single workflow that deploys all services in a rolling fashion as a release set and end to end tests that validates all services at once. This is partly due to a dependency on shared database schemas across services. Rolling back releases that contain db migrations after a deployment completes (without circuit breaker) requires significant development changes to deployment logic with implications to operational complexity.

risks.title: Survey Questionnaire multiple triggers
risks.description: Survey is triggering multiple times per day, including hundreds of instances sent by a service account

risks.title: Unvalidated Legal Tracker incident compression metrics may misrepresent AIOps benefits and hide missed incidents
risks.description: On 1-June-2026, Mike Krause presented preliminary Power BI analysis showing that average Legal Tracker incident volume appears to have dropped from ~91 incidents/day (1–19 May) to ~9 incidents/day (21–31 May) after Datadog-direct incident creation was commented out and Event Management incidents became the primary source. However, Mike and Paul Berry noted that these figures are currently anecdotal and depend on ad-hoc filters (e.g., treating incidents opened by "system administrator" as AIOps and by the Datadog service account as legacy) and on payload fields that the existing report does not yet parse (including some blank or differently shaped monitor IDs). There has been no systematic line-by-line validation to confirm that the 10x apparent compression accurately reflects duplicate/noise reduction without missing unique incidents.

risks.title: Worksoft-based Core regression testing cannot leverage external AI/LLMs
risks.description: In Core, approximately 85% of the regression test bed relies on Worksoft, a third-party tool that currently does not allow integration with external LLMs such as Claude or GPT. Worksoft’s own AI capabilities are limited, and any AI agent would have to be built within Worksoft itself. A replacement tool (e.g., Tosca) is now being actively considered to address this constraint.

risks.title: High-noise CPU utilisation monitors may hide capacity issues and distort AIOps behaviour
risks.description: Certain CPU utilisation monitors (e.g., "CPU is high on host" patterns) are generating very high alert volumes in Datadog and are frequently muted by product teams. In the 3-Jun-2026 sync, Legal Tracker examples showed warning-level CPU alerts that could indicate capacity problems but are either overly sensitive or routinely suppressed. These noisy monitors are candidates for both Datadog hygiene remediation and AIOps correlation tuning.

risks.title: Machine-learning-based AIOps grouping may incorrectly group unrelated Legal Tracker alerts
risks.description: ServiceNow AIOps machine-learning (ML)-driven alert grouping is combining unrelated Legal Tracker alerts (e.g., synthetic monitors and infrastructure monitors) into the same group based on text similarity and inferred CI relationships, even when impacted services differ. This behaviour is not controlled by Thomson Reuters’ explicit correlation rules and has already led to important infrastructure alerts being ‘hidden’ inside groups dominated by synthetic alerts.

risks.title: Insufficient CI/CMDB data quality and CI–service association may block broader onboarding despite ongoing remediation
risks.description: During the 28-May-2026 AIOps Product Onboarding regional sync, the team reconfirmed that unresolved CMDB health and CI–service association behaviour remain a gating factor for Legal Tracker and all downstream product onboardings. Subsequent working sessions (including the 8-June-2026 AIOps/Event Management regular sync) have shown that these issues also affect new early-adopter products such as ONESOURCE GTM4 and SIAM: many GTM4 configuration items referenced in Datadog alerts do not exist in the CMDB, and SIAM monitors are not linked to configuration items at all, forcing temporary workarounds (e.g., using the application as both configuration item and impacted service). Until a scalable CMDB remediation approach is implemented, applications will continue to have incomplete or incorrect CI and service mappings, limiting safe AIOps onboarding and cutover from legacy incident flows.

risks.title: Complex and inconsistent Datadog tagging standards may hinder adoption and correlation quality
risks.description: Current Datadog tagging standards and practices are complex and inconsistently applied across products. The Thomson Reuters tagging standards document defines many “required” tags (including multiple environment-related tags such as TR_environment_type, TR_environment_name, and nt_environment), but in practice product teams use different subsets and values, and many monitors have duplicate or conflicting tags (e.g., multiple environment tags on a single monitor, duplicate Asset Insight ID tags). During the 8-June-2026 AIOps/Event Management regular sync, Dominique and Mike highlighted that the environment tagging standards in the AIOps programme (e.g., TR_environment_type) differ from Datadog’s native ENV tag and that existing monitors already use ENV extensively. This complexity risks confusion and low compliance for new AIOps onboardings and undermines correlation rules that rely on specific TR_ tags.

risks.title: ServiceNow incident reopen behaviour and incident number changes may cause confusion and reporting issues
risks.description: ServiceNow Event Management is currently configured so that when a new alert group matches a previously closed incident, the platform reopens that incident and, in some observed cases, changes the incident number and unlinks/links alerts between incidents. This is out-of-the-box behaviour tied to alert grouping windows and incident-respond rules, but it is unfamiliar to Legal Tracker and GCC teams, who are used to static incident numbers and non-reopened incidents from the legacy Datadog→incident flow. The team considers the current deterministic incident-priority patch and this reopen behaviour an MVP to allow Legal Tracker to proceed, but has not yet decided whether this should become the long-term standard.

risks.title: Library Content backlog persists
risks.description: There is a risk that the existing Customer Trust (CT) content backlog persists, preventing timely review and update of tickets and knowledge base content.

risks.title: Delivery Quality measurement using AI Adoption Dashboard
risks.description: Until all platforms have consistent adoption reporting and data feeds (including GitHub, Claude, and other LLMs), delivery quality and efficiency tracking remains partially mixed and directional rather than definitive. Recent changes in data pipelines and data stores (e.g., decommissioning of the LLM data store and incorrect mapping of GitHub pull requests) introduce additional risk to the accuracy and completeness of AI adoption metrics.

risks.title: ServiceNow Zurich upgrade mid-May may constrain configuration changes and delay permanent fixes
risks.description: A ServiceNow Zurich upgrade is scheduled to start around mid-May (approx. May 16–17). Jot noted that there may be restrictions on what configuration changes can be made during this upgrade window, which coincides with ongoing work to stabilise incident priority behaviour, CI binding, and incident reopen behaviour for Legal Tracker.

risks.title: ServiceNow incident reopen and incident number change behaviour may confuse teams and distort reporting
risks.description: In the current AIOps/Event Management configuration, ServiceNow may reopen closed incidents and, in some cases, change the incident number when new alerts are grouped into existing alert groups. Legal Tracker stakeholders (Elizabeth and Andrea, via feedback to Luis Jorge) have observed that grouped alerts can reopen a previously closed incident and that the related incident number can change when alert links are updated. This behaviour is driven by default ServiceNow grouping and respond rules (e.g., 30-minute grouping window and incident creation on alert-group creation) and is not aligned with the team’s existing ways of working or reporting expectations.

risks.title: Insufficient SME and BISO participation in content governance and library management
risks.description: There is a risk that subject-matter experts (SMEs) and BISO contacts will not be able to commit sufficient time to content library management and the Content Governance process. Mitigation date: TBD at this time.

risks.title: Agent Chat go-live may impact SLAs due to untested high-volume routing behavior
risks.description: During the June 11, 2026 Agent Chat gap analysis call, Nitin highlighted that, in the current Vayusphere setup, all chats enter a single queue and are manually picked up by agents, with SMEs able to reassign chats to meet a 6–30 second SLA. In ServiceNow Advanced Work Assignment (AWA), chats are routed automatically based on capacity and skills, with a current 1-minute acceptance window and no equivalent SME override feature. Nitin expressed concern that, without volume testing and routing tuning (e.g., reduced acceptance window, auto-assignment), high chat volumes may not be routed correctly, leading to SLA breaches. He also noted that agents are new to the tool and that SLA exceptions may be needed for 2–3 months during transition. Jakub indicated he is open to SLA exceptions and suggested a phased rollout (e.g., APAC first) and possible parallel run with Vayusphere, but no detailed deployment plan is yet defined.

risks.title: Conversational greeting and fallback workflow may miss 2026-05-07 commitment
risks.description: The team committed to having a more natural, conversational virtual agent greeting, closing, and fallback experience ready by 2026-05-07, based on feedback from leaders (including Marc) that the current Now Assist chat lacks greetings, closing messages, validation, and ticket number sharing. During the 2026-05-05 SNOWNAWA working session, Shariq highlighted that there has been "no meaningful progress" on these conversational workflows, ownership is unclear (who raises the story, what Ashima and developers are working from), and admin access to edit templates is constrained. Although predefined templates and out-of-the-box system topics exist, they are not yet configured to meet the desired experience. If these items are not implemented and tested rapidly, the team may miss the 2026-05-07 target it has "given ourselves" for fixing the greetings and related chat behaviors.

risks.title: Onboarding products without monitors-as-code or bulk-update capability may delay rollout
risks.description: During the discussion, Elizabeth highlighted that Legal Tracker’s Datadog monitors are managed as code (Terraform/GitHub), which makes it easier to apply standardized changes (tags, priorities, handlers). Chris and Jot noted that effort estimates will differ for teams that do not manage monitors as code. Luis mentioned GCC has scripts to perform bulk operations against Datadog monitors but indicated this is a workaround and not the best long‑term approach. If new products lack monitors‑as‑code or bulk‑update capabilities, onboarding them to AIOps will require more manual changes per monitor (e.g., adding handlers, tags, correcting priorities), which could slow the rollout or result in inconsistent configurations.

risks.title: Lack of Agent Chat historical and current data in dashboards may impact governance reporting
risks.description: In the June 11, 2026 Agent Chat gap analysis discussion, Nitin noted that the dashboards currently used for governance and reporting rely on Vayusphere data, and that the new Agent Chat dashboard does not yet contain any data. He expressed concern that, until Agent Chat is actively used and/or historical data is migrated, HCL will be unable to produce monthly and hourly trending reports and other governance outputs from the Agent Chat portal. Saket and Nitin also discussed the possibility of migrating historical Vayusphere data into the Agent Chat dashboard, which Prashanth described as a separate data migration effort requiring analysis of tables and columns.

risks.title: Alert-threshold hygiene may be misreported if synthetic monitors are not excluded
risks.description: Nick and Dominique discussed that a "large chunk" of monitors show no alert threshold configured. Dominique clarified that, based on review with Tax, many of these are synthetic monitors, for which a traditional threshold is not expected. Current counting and reporting of "monitors without thresholds" does not filter out synthetics, which can overstate the problem and distort hygiene metrics.

risks.title: Potential negative impacts of reducing the number of Datadog organizations
risks.description: The program is considering whether to reduce the current number of Datadog organizations (110+). High complexity and several risks have been acknowledged, including possible loss of historical data, anomaly detection model resets, and AI/MCP rate‑limit or capacity impacts if organizations are consolidated without a carefully designed approach.

risks.title: Agent queue management governance between TR and HCL not defined
risks.description: The process and ownership for managing agent chat queues (e.g., adding new hires to language queues like French or English) has not been defined. Currently HCL self-manages queues in their existing setup, but it is unclear whether, and to what extent, they will have control within the TR ServiceNow (Advanced Work Assignment) configuration or if TR will centrally own this. Without clear governance, queue changes for new/changed agents may be slow or inconsistent.

risks.title: Knowledge base hygiene & scope creep
risks.description: Large volumes of legacy KB articles and unclear ownership, risking VA accuracy and MVP focus.

risks.title: Inconsistent IMC (incident) sharing behavior from agent chat
risks.description: An HCL team member observed that, after closing the chat, the incident (IMC) was not automatically shared back to the user as expected, despite recorded demos showing that it should be shared automatically when the agent creates the incident. The root cause is unclear (e.g., chat closed before saving, configuration differences, or defects).

risks.title: HCL may not commit effort or timelines for Amazon Connect – Virtual Agent integration
risks.description: Amazon Connect CTI migration from Avaya is essentially complete and is being tested, with CTI expected to show caller details in ServiceNow. However, integrating Amazon Connect with the virtual agent (e.g., for IVR-driven password reset and other flows) will require additional work from HCL. In the April 29, 2026 meeting, Shariq raised concern that HCL may view this as additional effort and could request 'a couple of weeks of effort' or otherwise delay or resist the integration, which affects the project’s IVR use cases.

risks.title: Delay in KB refresh planning and execution may impact Now Assist accuracy and timelines
risks.description: The detailed review and refresh of the ~500 prioritized service desk KB articles has not yet started. During the April 29, 2026 KB planning meeting, Shariq noted he will not be able to meaningfully progress this work until after the upcoming long weekend and is targeting Tuesday to have an executable plan. Until the review starts and decisions are made on which KBs to keep, update, merge, or archive, Now Assist will continue to use the existing, potentially outdated content set.

risks.title: Zurich upgrade and dev freeze may cause loss or rework of recent virtual agent and agent chat changes
risks.description: The upcoming Zurich upgrade will introduce a dev freeze period (May 8 to June 8) and a clone from production into the development environment. During the May 11, 2026 sync, Vinay explained that to avoid losing in-flight development work (especially virtual agent conversational workflows, plugins, and configuration changes), developers must take backups of update sets before the end of Friday. Srinu confirmed that some changes are already captured in update sets, but others (such as plugin enabling or certain configuration options) are not; these will need to be documented and manually re-applied after the clone. If backups and documentation are incomplete, recent VA and Agent Chat work could be overwritten or require significant rework after the clone, impacting timelines.

risks.title: Misalignment of Datadog default maturity scorecards with Thomson Reuters standards
risks.description: The team is exploring whether existing Datadog maturity scorecards can be used to measure observability maturity. Datadog’s default scorecards are generic and likely not aligned to Thomson Reuters’ internal observability and monitoring standards. If they are adopted without proper alignment or customization, measurements of maturity may be misleading or inconsistent across teams.

risks.title: Reliance on temporary customizations for incident priority and CI binding instead of AIOps-native behaviour
risks.description: To meet Legal Tracker timelines, the team has implemented temporary workarounds: (1) disabling out-of-the-box ServiceNow incident priority calculation and deterministically passing Datadog monitor priority straight through to incident priority; and (2) implementing temporary CI matching logic so that CI binding appears to work, even though underlying discovery/CMDB issues are unresolved. These changes diverge from ServiceNow AIOps standard design and are intended as MVP patches.

risks.title: Copilot live agent handoff and transcript sharing may not meet requirements
risks.description: The team is pivoting to Microsoft 365 Copilot as the interim conversational front end, but the live agent transfer capability from Copilot into ServiceNow Agent Chat has not yet been implemented or tested. Mayank and Shariq emphasized that for a good user experience, the entire Copilot conversation (or at least a useful summary) must be handed over to the ServiceNow live agent so that the agent can see the history and context. Today, the live agent functionality sits fully on the ServiceNow side, and it is unclear whether Copilot can reliably pass conversation history into the ServiceNow interaction/incident or whether an additional topic/API must be built specifically for live agent transfer. Until this is designed and validated, there is a risk that the handoff will be incomplete or fail altogether.

risks.title: Dynamic language translation capability may be lost when moving from Now Assist to Copilot
risks.description: Jakub and Shariq highlighted that the current dynamic language translation feature (used in Agent Chat to support non-English users while routing to English-speaking agents) relies on Now Assist capabilities. As the team pivots to Copilot as the front-end conversational agent, it is unclear whether equivalent dynamic translation will be available or how it will be implemented. Prastuti confirmed that Now Assist is required for the current AI-based real-time translation. If an alternative solution is not put in place, the project could lose the ability to offshore non-English traffic to the main support center while still providing localized experiences to users.

risks.title: Copilot-based solution may not preserve interaction linkage and history in ServiceNow
risks.description: Prastuti raised concern that, with Now Assist, conversational data is attached to the ServiceNow interaction and carried forward to incidents, enabling AWA-based features such as routing users back to the same agent within a time window. She noted that, with Copilot, TR will likely not store Copilot conversations as Virtual Agent conversations in ServiceNow by default. It is uncertain whether Copilot conversations will be linked to interaction/incident records in a way that preserves history and supports existing AWA capabilities (e.g., context-aware routing).

risks.title: Amazon Connect CTI URL misconfiguration may delay IVR demo and cutover
risks.description: During the May 11, 2026 Service Desk AI automation sync, Jakub and Saket reported an issue with the URL used by the Amazon Connect CTI integration: it currently opens an incident record populated with user details instead of an interaction record, whereas the desired behavior is to start from an interaction record. This misconfiguration is blocking completion of CTI testing and prevents scheduling the previously agreed Amazon Connect demo session for Wednesday. Saket stated that once the correct URL is provided and CTI testing is successful, the team will need an additional 2–3 business days to confirm testing, followed by approximately 10–14 days for the telco/ISP to change the external IVR numbers and perform cutover, with old numbers running in parallel for 2–3 weeks. Until the URL issue is resolved, these downstream steps cannot begin, putting IVR cutover timelines at risk.

risks.title: Delayed Playwright agent rollout in Core due to resource turnover
risks.description: In Core, the Playwright AI agent rollout is delayed because the automation engineer in Sumathi’s area resigned and a replacement FTE is only now being onboarded. Sumathi has requested time until mid-June to start the Playwright agent POC and subsequent implementation.

risks.title: Conversational greeting and fallback workflow may miss 2026-05-15 target due to customization constraints and vendor dependency
risks.description: The team has committed to delivering a complete conversational virtual agent workflow (including greetings when users do not start with "hi", handover behavior, and other feedback items) by 2026-05-15. Current testing shows that if a user types a problem directly (e.g., "my Outlook is crashing") without greeting the VA, the system does not send any greeting before giving a solution, which is considered poor user experience. Initial review on the prior Thursday suggested that achieving the desired greeting behavior may not be possible purely with out-of-the-box configuration and might require customization. During the May 11, 2026 sync, Vinay cautioned that custom scripting inside Now Assist / Virtual Agent is high risk for future upgrades and generally not recommended without ServiceNow guidance. The team is now dependent on multiple working sessions with the ServiceNow vendor (planned from Tuesday to Friday) to determine whether the required behavior can be achieved via configuration or safe customization. Until this is resolved, progress on several of the eight conversational workflow requirements remains blocked, increasing the risk that the agreed May 15 date will slip.

risks.title: Copilot integration behavior may change after MCP server and Zurich upgrade adjustments
risks.description: AD noted that, as part of the Zurich upgrade, an MCP server is being set up in the dev environment and that this may change slightly the experience and outcomes of current Copilot–ServiceNow integration tests. Mayank acknowledged this and expects it to help, but there is still uncertainty about how the new MCP setup and Zurich upgrade will affect existing Copilot prototypes and configurations.

risks.title: Agent chat dashboards and analytics requirements not yet defined
risks.description: HCL stakeholders requested dashboards to monitor agent chat performance (e.g., agent status, availability, queues in line). While the conversational analytics plugin can provide some out-of-the-box insights, custom dashboards must be built from scratch based on specific KPIs HCL wants to see. These KPIs and dashboard requirements have not yet been provided by HCL.

risks.title: Market‑Benchmarked Coding Efficiency Limits
risks.description: Coding efficiency improvements are market‑benchmarked at approximately 8–10%, making benefits planning and realization complex. Gains are incremental, distributed across multiple teams and tools, and not concentrated in a single measurable outcome, which complicates planning and value realization for the AI coding agents efficiency initiative.

risks.title: Insufficient engineering and architecture participation in the core working group
risks.description: The program raised the question of which engineering and architecture resources should be formally aligned to the core working group. Current attendees form the core team, but additional engineering participation is needed to provide sufficient implementation depth and coverage across domains.

risks.title: Delivery Quality measurement using AI Adoption Dashboard
risks.description: Until all data issues are resolved and platforms have consistent adoption reporting, delivery quality and efficiency tracking remains partially mixed and directional rather than definitive.

risks.title: Missing or blank Datadog Monitor IDs in ServiceNow payloads
risks.description: During progress on ServiceNow–Datadog incident correlation reporting, the team identified that some ServiceNow payloads contain missing or blank Datadog Monitor IDs. This gap affects the ability to correlate incidents to specific monitors and impacts the accuracy of the correlation MVP.

risks.title: Phase 1 backlog remains ungroomed and unprioritized
risks.description: April 14 notes and tracker actions indicate that the Phase 1 backlog (epics, features, and stories in Azure DevOps) requires cleanup and prioritization. Backlog grooming has been deferred to an offline working session.

risks.title: Event taxonomy for informational/warning/exception states may not be defined in time for Legal Tracker
risks.description: The target-state design depends on a clear event taxonomy that distinguishes informational, warning, and exception conditions so that ServiceNow Event Management can filter, classify, and prioritize events correctly. The Target Future State deck explicitly calls out that "Event taxonomy must be defined" as a dependency for filtering and classification rules. If this taxonomy is not defined and agreed before enabling broader AIOps behaviour for Legal Tracker, filtering and prioritization rules will be based on ad-hoc or inconsistent interpretations of monitor states.

risks.title: Data quality issues in correlation IDs and Datadog–ServiceNow mappings prevent reliable analytics
risks.description: Phase 1 discussions highlighted current data quality issues such as missing or inconsistent correlation IDs and gaps between Datadog alerts and ServiceNow incidents. These issues currently prevent reliable analysis and prioritization, and undermine the foundational analytics and dashboards needed for the program.

risks.title: HCL Vayusphere renewal decision may be misaligned with Agent Chat and Copilot timelines
risks.description: Jakub reminded the team that Vyas has a renewal with HCL this month and that HCL needs to know whether they should renew their existing Vayusphere chat solution. Kiran noted that Agent Chat as a Vayusphere replacement is "almost 95% done" and IVR work is also ongoing, while Shariq said they need a one-page view of options and impacts before deciding. If the Copilot and Agent Chat strategy is not clarified in time, HCL may either renew Vayusphere unnecessarily or face a gap without a supported chat solution.

risks.title: Absence of minimum alert standards constrains remediation
risks.description: The March 17 meeting recap explicitly noted that minimum alert standards do not yet exist. Without defined standards (e.g., required fields, service/asset associations, runbooks, thresholds), remediation work in Phase 1 is constrained and may be inconsistent across teams.

risks.title: Limited communication of the new monitoring review process beyond Problem Management
risks.description: April 14 meeting notes state that current communications about the new Datadog alert/monitoring review process have been internal to Problem Management. The need for broader communication to Service Management leadership, with cascade to their teams, was acknowledged.

risks.title: Monitoring effectiveness review process not yet fully operationalized
risks.description: The Datadog Alert & Monitor Effectiveness Review framework was introduced on April 7, with agreement to anchor it in Problem Tasks (P‑tasks). However, the review cadence is still being refined, and operationalization (including P‑task structure and review cadence) is pending alignment between Robin and Dominique.

risks.title: Recurring mis-mapping of Datadog P3 alerts to critical severity/P1 incidents in ServiceNow production
risks.description: During the 24-Apr-2026 AIOps Event Management regular sync, the team confirmed that alerts coming from Datadog with P3 priority are being created in ServiceNow as critical severity, which then drives P1 incident creation. Doug identified that the custom Datadog-to-Severity event field mapping script that worked in dev is not behaving correctly in production, likely due to rule ordering and interaction with other event mappings (e.g., synthetics). Until this is fixed, enabling automatic incident creation from alerts would generate a large number of false P1 incidents.

risks.title: SRE Agent: Unclear path to scaled benefits beyond initial scope
risks.description: The aggregate business value of the SRE Agent workstream is predicated on scaling beyond the initial product suite (LPP). There is currently no confirmed product roadmap or suitability assessment that provides a clear, sequenced line-of-sight into which additional products will benefit from automation, or when.

risks.title: SRE Agent: Unproven technology dependency
risks.description: The workstream places a strategic "big-bet" on AI agent technology that has not yet been validated in production SRE environments. The core automated remediation and runbook execution capabilities depend on cloud-native AI services (AWS) whose reliability, accuracy, and performance at scale remain unproven within the organization.

risks.title: DevOps: Diamond Lane Scale Readiness Risk – Incomplete Automation and Criteria Frameworks
risks.description: With 4 of 11 core milestones still in progress and ServiceNow policy integration intentionally deferred, there is a risk that Diamond Lane's CI criteria, product contracts, scorecard v1, and pipeline-driven change automation will not reach sufficient maturity by the 30 Jun 2026 target. This could prevent the program from enforcing eligibility and routing decisions in an auditable, repeatable way before broader application onboarding begins.

risks.title: DevOps Diamond Lane – Limited '26 Product Coverage and VC Benefit Realization
PLE Phased Benefits Realization Plan Delivery Pending
risks.description: A high-level benefits delivery plan is in place. A phased plan is in progress, with initial confirmed benefits realization expected in June. However, there is currently no period/quarter-level visibility into the benefits delivery schedule. The absence of granular planning creates uncertainty around tracking, reporting, and on-time realization of PLE program benefits.

risks.title: Salesforce Coding Assistant / Agentforce licensing and low adoption
risks.description: As of June 1, 2026, Agentforce (Agent Force Vibes) became a licensed tool and all existing developer access was cut off, impacting ~45 Salesforce developers who had been using it for AI-assisted development. Licensing decisions (whether to purchase Agentforce licenses or standardize on an alternative such as GitHub Copilot or another TR-approved AI tool) remain unresolved, while teams temporarily experiment with GitHub Copilot and OpenArena. This compounds the existing low-adoption issue for the Salesforce Coding Assistant and creates uncertainty around a stable, approved AI coding tool for Salesforce.

risks.title: Parallel onboarding of GTM4 and SIAM may overextend capacity and delay effective onboarding
risks.description: The team plans to onboard both ONESOURCE GTM4 and SIAM in parallel as the next AIOps adopters. During the 11 May 2026 sync, Mike Krause raised concern that GTM4 generates a high volume of alerts and will likely produce many findings and follow-up work. Although he is not opposed to onboarding two products in parallel, he is conscious that resource and attention demands could be significant, particularly while the team is still resolving early issues from the Legal Tracker pilot.

risks.title: ETS VC Targets
risks.description: ServiceDesk case does not have a firm roadmap in place on how VC outcomes will be achieved in 2027 regarding HCL Insource/Renegotiation. Latest feedback from team was a revision of savings estimate to ~$1.5M annualized, down from $3M.

risks.title: Limited Loopio API technical information may lead to incorrect assumptions and integration constraints
risks.description: There is a risk that limited understanding of Loopio’s API capabilities leads to incorrect technical assumptions, integration constraints, security approval delays, or unplanned re-architecture.

risks.title: Insufficient CI/CMDB data quality and CI binding for effective correlation and routing
risks.description: Many incoming events lack reliable CI bindings due to inconsistent or missing metadata, such as FQDNs for Azure VMs, host/node field gaps, and inconsistent tag usage. CI mapping is often at service level only, and HighQ and other products rely heavily on tags and Asset Insight IDs. If CI binding issues are not resolved, correlation, grouping, and routing in ServiceNow will be inaccurate.

risks.title: PMOP: Post‑Pilot Support & Capacity Risk
risks.description: After Tiger Team rolls off, PMO Partner depends on existing AI Services capacity with no incremental resourcing, while simultaneously absorbing pilot bugs, MVP gaps, and fast‑follow features. This creates a risk of backlog stagnation and delayed fixes if PMO Partner competes with other EAIS priorities.

risks.title: Insufficient AIOps engineering capacity and access to scale onboarding to multiple applications
risks.description: Current AIOps onboarding and configuration work for Legal Tracker, ONESOURCE GTM4 and SIAM is heavily dependent on a single engineer (Rodriguez, Luis Jorge). During the 26-May-2026 AIOps Product Onboarding regular sync, Talia and Jot highlighted that scaling to 5–6 applications per month or per week is unrealistic with the existing capacity, even before addressing CMDB issues. Although additional engineers (e.g., Vijay, Mahesha, Owen, Erikipaty) have been identified as potential contributors, they do not yet have Event Management admin access in ServiceNow, and their roles and responsibilities in the AIOps program are not fully defined. Without increased and properly permissioned engineering capacity, onboarding timelines for the FY 2026 roadmap will slip and the program will not be able to meet leadership expectations for scale.

risks.title: Machine-learning-based alert grouping may incorrectly group unrelated Legal Tracker alerts
risks.description: ServiceNow AIOps machine-learning (ML)–driven alert grouping is combining unrelated Legal Tracker alerts (e.g., a synthetic monitor and an infrastructure monitor) into the same alert group based on CI relationships, even when impacted services differ. These ML-created groups are not using the TR-defined correlation rules. If ML continues to group dissimilar alerts, incidents derived from these groups may represent multiple distinct issues, and teams will see inconsistent, hard-to-explain behaviour in Event Management.

risks.title: ServiceNow event forwarding limits may cause loss of events in lower environments
risks.description: ServiceNow event forwarding from production to lower environments (dev/QA) appears subject to a per-day forwarding limit and a one-hour event duration window. Yash raised a concern that, under the current configuration, older events outside the one-hour window may not be forwarded, creating a risk that some Datadog-originating events will never reach dev/QA for rule testing and correlation validation.

risks.title: Incident creation policy and notification tiers may not be agreed before event-first processing is enabled
risks.description: The Target Future State and capability prioritization highlight open design decisions around incident creation policy (which events should create incidents vs remain as events or trigger auto-remediation) and notification tiers (what severity warrants after-hours paging vs next-business-day notification). These are listed as later-phase design items, yet the routing and resolution stages of the target lifecycle depend on them. If incident creation policy and notification tiers are not agreed before enabling broader event-first processing for Legal Tracker, incidents and on-call pages may not reflect true business impact.

risks.title: Insufficient CI/CMDB data quality and CI/service association may block broader onboarding despite ongoing remediation
risks.description: During the 28-May-2026 AIOps Product Onboarding regional sync, the team reconfirmed that unresolved CMDB health and CIservice association behaviour remain a gating factor for Legal Tracker and all downstream product onboardings. Talia reiterated that the new ServiceNow resource (Bill) has proposed an approach to address the CI/service association problem (including the current configurable ~1,000-CI-per-service parameter and overall service mapping strategy), and that a detailed pre-read and action plan are expected for the 4-June session. AD and Eric explicitly questioned whether the magnitude of the CMDB problem is being underestimated and noted that if the CI/service association issue is not understood and fixed, it will halt implementation for additional applications and jeopardize the September onboarding roadmap. Jot highlighted that any approach which relies on application teams to validate and reduce their CI sets could introduce significant lift and delay, because most teams lack mature documentation and would need to manually validate which CIs are actually consumed by their processes. The team agreed that CMDB health and service mapping must become an explicit prerequisite and part of the onboarding process for each application, and that the feasibility of the multimonth roadmap depends directly on the outcome of Bills design and the CMDB teams capacity to execute it.

actions.description: Based on the ML configuration parameters received from the ServiceNow team, adjust similarity thresholds or other settings for the text-based ML alert grouping so that unrelated alerts (e.g., Legal Tracker synthetics and disk/CPU infrastructure monitors with different impacted services) are no longer grouped together. If acceptable behaviour cannot be achieved quickly, coordinate with the ServiceNow platform team to disable this specific text-based ML grouping for Legal Tracker to prevent further operational impact.

actions.title: Investigate ServiceNow incident UI options to display all alerts in a group on the incident record
actions.description: Work with the ServiceNow platform/engineering team to determine whether the incident form for AIOps-generated incidents can be configured to show all alerts in the related alert group (and the total group size), rather than only the primary alert, so that support engineers can easily see hidden alerts such as disk/CPU monitors that are currently obscured by grouped synthetics.

actions.title: Emphasize use of Event Management Express List for Legal Tracker and future onboarded teams during observation period
actions.description: Update onboarding and communication for Legal Tracker, GTM4, SIAM, and subsequent products to explicitly instruct support engineers to use the Event Management Express List view during the observation/parallel run period, so they can see all grouped and orphan alerts (including single-occurrence disk/CPU warnings) instead of relying solely on incident records.

actions.title: Raise noisy Legal Tracker CPU monitor behaviour into Datadog hygiene and AIOps governance forums
actions.description: Escalate the observed noisy Legal Tracker CPU monitor (frequent high-CPU alerts that are often muted) into the Datadog hygiene and AIOps governance discussions, ensuring that the owning product/infra team reviews thresholds, mute patterns, and capacity implications so that the monitor either reflects genuine risk or is tuned to reduce unnecessary alert volume.

actions.title: Clarify FedRAMP requirement to disable AI training data and implications for AIOps
actions.description: Review historical notes and governance guidance to confirm the requirement to disable AI training data in the FedRAMP ServiceNow environment, and document the rationale and implications for AIOps capabilities (e.g., ML-based grouping). Provide this clarification to ROE, TIM (TR Technology) so that AI training settings can be configured correctly when porting AIOps/Event Management configuration into FedRAMP.

actions.title: Review and mirror AIOps/Event Management configuration into FedRAMP instance
actions.description: Review all AIOps/Event Management modules and configurations that were enabled in the enterprise ServiceNow instance and plan how to mirror the necessary configurations into the FedRAMP ServiceNow environment, ensuring compliance with FedRAMP constraints.

actions.title: Reduce Advanced Work Assignment chat acceptance timeout for Agent Chat
actions.description: Update ServiceNow Advanced Work Assignment (AWA) configuration so that Agent Chat offers are not held with a single agent for 60 seconds. Reduce the chat acceptance timeout to approximately 10–30 seconds (targeting 10 seconds if technically feasible) so that if an agent does not accept an interaction promptly, it is automatically re-assigned to another available agent, supporting HCL’s SLA expectations (6–30 seconds to pick up chats).

actions.title: Validate updated Agent Chat routing configuration and dashboards with HCL leads and confirm sign-off
actions.description: After TR implements the reduced AWA timeout and other routing changes, coordinate with HCL leads to (1) test the new routing behavior, (2) confirm that dashboard metrics on the Agent Chat dashboards meet operational needs, and (3) draft and send a formal email (via Saket Behl) confirming Agent Chat readiness, including a request for 2–3 months of SLA exceptions during the migration period.

actions.title: Capture bulk transcript download requirement in Agent Chat gap analysis tracker
actions.description: Record the requirement raised by Ammini Anand to download Agent Chat transcripts in bulk (for all chats handled by an agent or team over a given period) in the Agent Chat gap analysis/requirements tracker so it is formally tracked and prioritized with other must-haves before sign-off.

actions.title: Update Agent Chat gap analysis Excel with test cases, must-haves, and new SLA concerns
actions.description: Review and update the Agent Chat gap analysis Excel file with (1) all current test cases and must-have requirements, and (2) the newly discussed SLA and routing concerns (including the mitigation plan to reduce AWA timeout). Add a separate tab summarizing Nitin Sinha’s concerns and Prashanth’s mitigation so they are visible to all stakeholders.

issues.title: Missing or blank Datadog Monitor IDs in ServiceNow payloads
issues.description: Some ServiceNow incidents generated from Datadog alerts are missing or have blank Datadog Monitor IDs in their payloads, causing gaps in incident‑to‑monitor correlation.

issues.title: ServiceNow CI binding not working as expected for Legal Tracker events
issues.description: Events ingested from Datadog into ServiceNow are not automatically associating to existing CIs in the CMDB, even when matching CI names exist, causing CI binding to fail for many events.

issues.title: Governance difficulty with 110+ Datadog organizations
issues.description: The current landscape includes more than 110 Datadog organizations, making centralized governance significantly harder and raising questions about whether consolidation is needed.

issues.title: Potential duplicate/incidental increase during AIOps cutover
issues.description: Enabling AIOps‑driven incident creation while leaving existing Datadog→ServiceNow incident integrations active could temporarily increase incident counts or create near‑duplicate incidents until Datadog incident creation is disabled.

issues.title: AIOps-generated incidents breaching response SLA due to closure before acknowledgement
issues.description: Legal Tracker incidents created via the AIOps/Event Management pipeline are sometimes being resolved/closed without an acknowledgement step, leading to response SLA breaches even though the incidents are ultimately resolved. Andrea observed that incidents show as resolved but still appear as having breached SLA, and Luis suspects the response SLA is breaking because incidents are being closed before acknowledgement.

issues.title: Current use case level plan is short of target $3.3M committed
issues.description: The current use case–level plan for AI initiatives does not yet reach the committed $3.3M benefits target, requiring identification of additional use cases to close the gap.

issues.title: Asset ID data quality gap in Datadog monitors
issues.description: A significant portion of Datadog monitors lack associated Asset IDs, creating a critical data quality gap that undermines monitor-to-asset correlation and limits the effectiveness of Datadog hygiene analytics and remediation.

issues.title: ServiceNow event forwarding limits may drop older events during lower-environment testing
issues.description: ServiceNow event forwarding from production to lower environments operates with a per-day forwarding limit and a one-hour duration window, and does not backfill historical events. As confirmed in the ServiceNow Support HiCase reviewed on 30-Apr-2026, this behaviour risks losing events older than one hour and may prevent complete event streams from being forwarded to dev/QA for AIOps rule testing.

issues.title: Loopio self-service tool AI enablement feature missing
issues.description: The AI enablement feature in the Loopio self-service tool is not yet turned on, leading to more manual research work for Customer Trust customers and team members.

issues.title: ServiceNow AIOps machine learning grouping is combining unrelated Legal Tracker alerts
issues.description: ServiceNow AIOps machine learning is grouping Legal Tracker alerts that should not be grouped together (e.g., a synthetic monitor alert and an infrastructure monitor alert with different impacted services). These ML-created groups bypass the Thomson Reuters–defined correlation rules, causing inconsistent alert grouping behaviour for Legal Tracker.

issues.title: GCC lacks access to ServiceNow Event Management for Legal Tracker alerts
issues.description: The GCC manager for Legal Tracker (Rajendran Van) and GCC analysts do not currently have access to the ServiceNow Event Management module and cannot see or work with Legal Tracker alert groups. Only Rodriguez, Luis Jorge is currently reviewing alerts in Event Management for Legal Tracker.

issues.title: Missing or incorrect service associations in AIOps-generated incidents for Legal Tracker
issues.description: Incidents created through the ServiceNow AIOps/Event Management pipeline for Legal Tracker are missing or incorrectly populated service associations (impacted service fields). As a temporary workaround, incident priority and service are being passed directly from Datadog monitors, but a long-term, platform-native fix for impacted service mapping is still being designed and implemented.

issues.title: Confusing incident reopen behaviour and incident number changes for AIOps-generated incidents
issues.description: For Legal Tracker, incidents created via the ServiceNow AIOps/Event Management pipeline are being reopened when new alert groups arrive and, in some cases, the incident number changes and related alerts are unlinked from prior incidents. This behaviour is confusing Legal Tracker stakeholders and may impact historical tracking and reporting.

issues.title: CI binding now working but CI–service association limits remain a concern
issues.description: Following recent discovery and CI-binding fixes by Kolluru, Prudhvi Yaswanth, CI binding for Legal Tracker assets is expected to work as intended (no active VMs in retired state, discovery failures remediated, and custom logic deactivated). However, a ServiceNow limitation on the number of CI associations per application service (around 1,000 CIs) may still prevent correct service association for large applications using tag-based service mappings.

issues.title: ServiceNow AIOps machine learning text-based grouping continues to incorrectly combine Legal Tracker alerts, causing operational impact
issues.description: ServiceNows text-based machine-learning alert grouping is still grouping unrelated Legal Tracker alerts into a single alert group based on similarities in alert descriptions and titles, even when the alerts come from different monitor types (e.g., synthetics vs disk/CPU infrastructure) and have different impacted services. In at least one recent case, a disk-usage alert was grouped under a synthetic primary alert, causing the disk issue to be effectively hidden within the group and contributing to a major situation for Legal Tracker.

issues.title: Inconsistent alert grouping for Legal Tracker due to AI/ML-based CI relationship grouping
issues.description: ServiceNows machine-learning-based event correlation is grouping unrelated Legal Tracker alerts into a single alert group based on inferred CI relationships, including combining a synthetic monitor alert and an infrastructure monitor alert even when impacted services differ. These ML-created groups are not aligned with the TR-defined correlation rules agreed for Legal Tracker.

issues.title: Incident reopening and incident number changes for AIOps-generated incidents
issues.description: For Legal Tracker, incidents created via the ServiceNow AIOps/Event Management pipeline are being reopened and, in some cases, assigned new incident numbers when additional alerts are grouped into an existing alert group. Related alerts are being unlinked from previous incidents and attached to new ones, causing confusion for operators and complicating historical tracking and reporting.

issues.title: CI binding and CI–service association still failing for Legal Tracker after attempted fixes
issues.description: Despite earlier statements that discovery issues were fixed and CI binding should now work, sample checks during the April 30, 2026 AIOps Product Onboarding regional sync showed that recent Legal Tracker alerts in ServiceNow are still missing CI bindings and/or are associated to incorrect services. A suspected ServiceNow product limitation (approximately 1,000 CIs per service) and incomplete follow-up with ServiceNow and internal platform teams are contributing factors.

issues.title: GCC team lacks access to ServiceNow Event Management for Legal Tracker alerts
issues.description: The GCC manager for Legal Tracker (Rajendran Van) and GCC operators do not currently have access to the ServiceNow Event Management workspace, so they cannot see or work Legal Tracker alerts created by AIOps. Luis has explained the application behaviour to GCC, but access has not yet been provisioned.

issues.title: AIOps-generated incident priorities are higher than corresponding alert priorities
issues.description: Incidents created by ServiceNow AIOps from group alerts are being assigned higher priorities (often P1) than expected based on the underlying alert severity and priority. Analysis of the 'create incident TR presets' subflow and related flow actions shows that incident impact and urgency are set to their highest values whenever the alert priority group or severity is 1 or 2, which forces the incident priority matrix to produce P1 incidents. In addition, the alert 'priority group' field is driven by an out-of-the-box priority score that may not align with Thomson Reuters expectations, and current event rules map Datadog monitor priority into alert severity but do not explicitly map priority into the alert priority group. As a result, Legal Tracker alerts with moderate priorities (e.g., P3) can still generate P1 incidents, causing misaligned incident priorities compared to direct Datadog-created incidents.

issues.title: Agentforce licensing removal blocks Salesforce developers from AI assistance
issues.description: Agentforce (Agent Force Vibes) became a licensed tool as of June 1, 2026, and licenses for approximately 45 Salesforce developers have been removed. As a result, developers can no longer use Agentforce for AI-assisted development, and teams are temporarily switching to GitHub Copilot and OpenArena while leadership evaluates whether to purchase Agentforce licenses or standardize on an alternative tool.

issues.title: Datadog P3 alerts mapped as critical severity in ServiceNow alerts for Legal Tracker
issues.description: In the ServiceNow production instance, Legal Tracker alerts coming from Datadog with monitor priority P3 are being mapped to critical severity on the ServiceNow alert records. As a result, incidents created from these alerts appear as P1, even though the underlying Datadog monitors are configured as P3. The problem appears to originate in the custom ServiceNow event field mapping rule "Datadog map alert priority to severity" not behaving as it did in dev, potentially due to rule ordering or execution context.

issues.title: ServiceNow license renewal and Now Assist license mapping blocking AI capabilities on new instance
issues.description: ServiceNow license renewal and license mapping between the legacy and new instances are preventing Now Assist and related AI capabilities from being enabled on the new ServiceNow instance. The license team has confirmed that licenses are still effectively tied to the legacy instance, causing the Now Assist mapping on the new instance to be disconnected. As a result, ongoing work on Agent Chat enhancements, Amazon Connect CTI URL fixes, and other Now Assist/virtual agent features is currently on hold until the renewal discussion is resolved and licenses are properly applied to the new instance.

 Mitigation date: TBD as this is an ongoing knowledge transfer and project planning effort.

issues.title: Datadog to ServiceNow production OAuth authentication failures (401 errors)
issues.description: After pointing the Datadog webhook to the ServiceNow production instance, Datadog receives HTTP 401 responses when attempting to send events, indicating authentication/authorization failures.

issues.title: Some HCL pilot users cannot access Agent Chat widget despite being in NAVA pilot group
issues.description: A subset of HCL pilot users (e.g., Kandibanda, Rakesh and Sri Lakshmi) cannot see or use the Agent Chat widget in ServiceNow, even though they are members of the NAVA pilot group and others in the same group have working access. This is causing inconsistent testing coverage for Agent Chat.

issues.description: Blocks Agent Chat and related SNOW integrations. Requires ServiceNow code changes + impacted by dev freeze

issues.description: Some reviewers lack sufficient knowledge to effectively review and maintain Loopio library content, reducing review quality and efficiency.

issues.title: NAVA / ServiceNow issue
issues.description: Assistants are not showing to restore the data after clone, and resolution is now additionally constrained by ServiceNow license renewal and license mapping between the legacy and new instances, which prevent enabling Now Assist capabilities on the new instance.

issues.title: Synthetic monitors inflate reported count of monitors without alert thresholds
issues.description: Current analytics count monitors without alert thresholds without distinguishing synthetic monitors, leading to a reported figure of 20–30% of monitors lacking thresholds. The majority of these are synthetic monitors, for which the absence of a threshold is expected, causing the analytics to overstate the true threshold gap.

issues.title: Lack of Datadog monitor metadata in inventory exports blocks team-level cleanup
issues.description: Current Datadog inventory exports (e.g., those produced by Jacob Kinsa) lack critical metadata such as who created each monitor, who it is assigned to, and when it last fired. Dashboard failure after clone due to Performance Analytics / analytics plugin issue; reinstall/repair attempts did not fully resolve it in the current environment.

risks.title: GTM4 Content PROD Cluster Migration
risks.description:
The GTM4 Content PROD environment includes three critical content clusters with high customer dependency. Migrating these clusters requires re‑initializing database replication from scratch, which is time‑consuming and highly sensitive to maintenance windows. There is a risk that replication may not complete within the agreed downtime window. Similar challenges were experienced during the earlier on‑prem to cloud migration, where replication delays caused operational issues.
Additionally, a future GCP content migration is already planned, which may require repeating the same replication process—potentially resulting in two customer downtimes if not carefully planned.
Risk Impact:
Potential extended PROD downtime impacting customers
Increased operational and reputational risk if replication fails or overruns
Need for multiple customer downtimes (current migration + future GCP migration)
Possible schedule changes to GTM4 Phase / Wave execution
Minor cost impact (~$4.5K/month) if clusters are retained longer as‑is, but operational risk outweighs cost considerations.
Risk Probability:
Medium – based on past replication challenges and dependency complexity, pending business decision. 
Current Status / Decision Pending:
Risk logged primarily as a decision risk
Business discussion scheduled to assess tolerance for downtime vs. deferring migration
Final approach may change based on Business Unit agreement
Mitigation / Next Steps:
Review and align with the Business Unit on acceptable downtime and migration approach
Explore deferring migration of these clusters to align with future GCP migration, avoiding double downtime
Document final business decision in ADO and update RAID accordingly (close or re‑categorize risk) 
Owner
GTM Business

milestones.description:
CIO-sponsored strategic transformation aligned with Product Engineering to deliver cloud portability and modernize TR’s application estate. The program targets migration of ~59 applications across ~18 product families from AWS to GCP over a 30‑month, wave-based roadmap—enabling platform consolidation, AI-ready foundations, and sustained service reliability across GTM, IDT, DT, and Data Hub.
Milestone Status:
Program Initiation and Planning completed on 10-Apr-2026 as planned. Foundations and Landing Zone phase is in progress and on track for 22-Jun-2026 completion under Google’s 16-week engagement. Pilot selection is underway, with Constellation confirmed and key dependencies (DevSecOps toolchain, wave planning) tracking to Jun’26 milestones.
Overall Health: Green — delivery progressing to plan.

Program is currently in Foundation Architecture & Landing Zone Ready phase with key dependencies in-flight. Google’s 16‑week Cloud Foundations is underway, and the teams have completed the initial 3‑day foundational workshops (architecture, security posture, network topology). Program is now progressing through follow‑up Landing Zone and Networking decision sessions, closing architecture, security, tagging, and CI/CD decisions while advancing toward Infrastructure‑as‑Code (IaC) build and deployment through late June. Accenture SOW is finalized, awaiting confirmation.

Pilot workload selection is underway for a Jun-Aug window, with Constellation confirmed as the first pilot and supporting dependencies such as DevSecOps toolchain decisions and wave planning tracking against Jun'26 target dates.

Overall status is Green, with Foundations and Landing Zone progressing well to plan.
